17150.text: Rebelling against God's Spirit [D1]: "they rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit" (Isa 63:10); "stubborn children … who make an alliance, but not of my Spirit" (Isa 30:1); "whoever disregards this, disregards … God, who gives his Holy Spirit to you" (1Th 4:8); "the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah … 'Because you have forsaken the Lord, he has forsaken you'" (2Ch 24:20)

17158.text: 9.4 Despising and rejecting — heart and soul as agents: "she despised him in her heart" (2Sa 6:16; 1Ch 15:29) — Michal; "How I hated discipline, and my heart despised reproof!" (Pro 5:12); "Whoever ignores instruction despises himself [*his nephesh*]" (Pro 15:32); "if your soul abhors my rules" (Lev 26:15); "their soul abhorred my statutes" (Lev 26:43); "the wicked … renounces God and says in his heart, 'You will not call to account'" (Psa 10:13; 10:3); "their heart went after their idols" (Eze 20:16)

17160.text: Refusal as the soul's own act: "my soul refuses to be comforted" (Psa 77:2); "My appetite refuses to touch them" (Job 6:7).

17166.text: God's heart vs man's eyes: "I have rejected him … the Lord looks on the heart" (1Sa 16:7).

17174.text: 11. Cross-cutting observations for Batch C [Claude reading]: The soul is the desiring self. In the OT, *nephesh* is the ordinary subject of "want / crave / long / thirst", from appetite for meat (Deu 12:20) to thirst for God (Psa 42:1–2). The same *nephesh* is the life that enemies seek (§7.5) and the life that is precious (§1.7). Desire and vitality are one word.; The heart is where orientation is set, held, divided or hardened. It plans, forms intentions, resolves, seeks, turns, is whole or not whole, and is stubborn or hardened. Many of these are expressed as setting / directing / inclining the heart (1Sa 7:3; Jos 24:23; 2Ch 19:3; 30:19). This extends Batch B's "attention = setting the heart" into will.; The human spirit carries energy and disposition, more than choice. It is "moved" to give (Exo 35:21), "fervent" (Rom 12:11), "willing" against weak flesh (Mat 26:41), patient or proud (Ecc 7:8), ruled (Pro 16:32), hardened with the heart (Deu 2:30), not faithful (Psa 78:8), and crushed or contrite (Psa 34:18; 51:17). Planning and choosing are rarely predicated of the human spirit [observation, not a count].; Heart and spirit are paired in the orientation verses (Exo 35:21; Deu 2:30; Psa 51:17; 78:8; Isa 57:15; Eze 11:19; 36:26). Heart and soul are paired in the "all your heart and all your soul" formula for seeking and returning (Deu 4:29; 1Ki 8:48; 2Ch 15:12).; Flesh changes role across the corpus.; OT: flesh longs and faints for God with the soul (Psa 63:1; 84:2). The "heart of flesh" is God's gift (Eze 36:26).; NT: flesh is the main subject of wrong desire (Gal 5:16–17; 1Jo 2:16), set against the Spirit and the soul (1Pe 2:11) and weak beside a willing spirit (Mat 26:41).; 2Co 3:3 ("tablets of fleshly hearts") keeps the OT positive use inside the NT.; God's Spirit relates to orientation as giver and as the one resisted.; Giver: good Spirit leading (Psa 143:10), patience (Gal 5:22), hope (Rom 5:5; 15:13), received on repentance (Act 2:38).; Resisted: rebelled against and grieved (Isa 63:10), disregarded (1Th 4:8), bypassed in plans (Isa 30:1).; The Spirit also desires against the flesh (Gal 5:17) and wills (1Co 12:11).

17175.text: 11. Cross-cutting observations for Batch C [Claude reading]: God is shown with his own soul and heart of desire and choice: his soul delights in the chosen servant (Isa 42:1), his heart is set on the chosen house (2Ch 7:16), he seeks a man after his heart (1Sa 13:14), his heart is grieved (Gen 6:6).; Other spirits in this batch act on orientation from outside: spirit of jealousy (Num 5), spirit of whoredom (Hos 4:12; 5:4) [X]; harmful spirit from God (1Sa 16) and the spirit at work in the disobedient (Eph 2:2) [O]; the unclean spirit seeking a dwelling (Mat 12:43) [O].; Fringe worth keeping: desire as breath-hunger — "striving after wind" (§1.9); the wine-merry heart as the point of exposure (§1.6); the heart that forsakes its owner (§9.6); the spirit that cannot be retained (Ecc 8:8); fleshly vs spiritual, with its moral / neutral / positive senses (§3.3); the heart awake while the body sleeps (Song 5:2)

17178.text: The glorified-body verses exist (Php 3:21; 1 Cor 15:43-53; 2 Cor 5:1-4) and sit in Ch 2.

17181.text: Tit 2:7 (the imperishable said of the inner person, with integrity in teaching) and Php 3:11 (that by any means possible I may attain the resurrection from the dead; Php 3:10 is in Ch 14) were proposed in the OT-05.26 reading and not woven: two small gaps.

17182.text: The glorified body is in the verses, but none of them carries an M47 word: who will transform our lowly body to be like his glorious body (Php 3:21); it is sown in dishonor, raised in glory, raised a spiritual body (1 Cor 15:43-44); this perishable body must put on the imperishable (15:53); a building from God, a house not made with hands (2 Cor 5:1-4). They are told in Ch 2 as death and resurrection, not as the body.

17186.text: The body as where fear and anguish show, through the hands: Jer 6:24; 50:43; Isa 13:7-8; Eze 7:17; 21:7; Jer 30:6; Zep 3:16; Neh 6:9; 2 Sam 4:1 (his courage failed, literally his hands dropped); Isa 35:3; Job 4:3; Heb 12:12; Lam 4:6; the flesh and body reading picks it up as the body's outward side.

17189.text: Unity and division: one heart, one soul, one flesh; a double heart (Psa 86:11; Psa 12:2; Gal 5:17).

17192.text: Opposition: flesh against Spirit in the NT (Gal 5:16-17); in the OT flesh is frail, not hostile (Isa 31:3).

17211.text: Inside one person, perplexity leads to a question, then waiting for an interpreter (Act 10:17-19).

17218.text: What changes or stops an operation: an interpreter arriving (Luk 24:4; Act 2:14).

17223.text: Method 3 of carrying an inner operation, an inner place outside M47 (a body word or pronoun), internal: chob, bosom (Job 31:33); chambers of the belly (Pro 18:8); in himself (Act 10:17); within him (Est 1:12).

17226.text: An inner operation without an explicit seat is carried by another person naming the seat: Jezebel to Ahab, God to Cain, Jesus in Luk 24:38.

17233.text: a. The heart as "centre / midst": The same word names the middle of non-human things: "the heart of the seas" (Eze 27:4, 25, 26, 27; 28:2, 8; Jon 2:3; Psa 46:2; Exo 15:8); "the heart of heaven" (Deu 4:11); "the heart of the earth" (Mat 12:40); "the midst of the sea" (Pro 23:34); fringe [Claude reading]: the inner seat is named with the ordinary word for *the middle of something*. A person's heart is their "midst".

17234.text: b. The physical heart and the chest: Arrows and javelins pierce it (2Ki 9:24; 2Sa 18:14; Psa 45:5; 37:15).; God will "tear open their breast" (Hos 13:8).; Aaron bears the names of Israel and the Urim and Thummim *"on his heart"*, on the breastpiece (Exo 28:29–30).; fringe [Claude reading]: the physical place and the inner seat are one word. Aaron's breastpiece is a physical act of *carrying people on one's heart before the Lord*.

17235.text: c. Inner speech — the heart as the place one "says" things: "Said in his heart / to himself": Gen 17:17; 24:45; 27:41; 1Ki 12:26; 1Sa 27:1; Deu 7:17; 8:17; 9:4; 18:21; Psa 10:6, 11, 13; 14:1; 53:1; Isa 14:13; 47:8, 10; 49:21; Jer 5:24; 13:22; Obd 3; Zep 1:12; 2:15; Est 6:6; Ecc 1:16; 2:1, 15; 3:17–18; Rom 10:6; Rev 18:7.; Hannah "was speaking in her heart; only her lips moved" (1Sa 1:13).; "Before I had finished speaking in my heart" (Gen 24:45).; The *content* of heart-speech is often self-assessment or self-deception: "I shall not be moved" (Psa 10:6); "There is no God" (Psa 14:1); "My power … has gotten me this wealth" (Deu 8:17); "I am, and there is no one besides me" (Isa 47:8; Zep 2:15).; Nehemiah "took counsel with *myself*" (Neh 5:7, lēv); "Ask *yourself*" style reflexives also appear.

17236.text: d. Thinking, planning, understanding, remembering: *Plans and devising:* Pro 16:1, 9; 19:21; 6:14, 18; 24:2; 12:20; Psa 140:2; 58:2; Zec 7:10; 8:17; Isa 10:7; Act 5:4; Eze 38:10.; *Understanding and knowing:*; "a heart to understand" (Deu 29:4); "understanding mind" (1Ki 3:9); "understand with their hearts" (Isa 6:10; Mat 13:15; Joh 12:40; Act 28:27); "an intelligent heart acquires knowledge" (Pro 18:15); "the heart of the hasty will understand" (Isa 32:4); *Remembering and "laying to heart":*; Isa 47:7; 57:1, 11; 42:25; Mal 2:2; Jer 12:11; Ecc 7:2; 9:1; Deu 4:39; 32:46; 1Sa 21:12; "call to mind" (Lam 3:21; Deu 30:1); "come into mind" (Jer 3:16; 7:31; 19:5; 32:35; 44:21; 51:50; Isa 65:17); Haggai's repeated "Consider your ways" is literally *set your heart* (Hag 1:5, 7; 2:15, 18) [lexical].; *Searching and investigating:* "I applied my heart to seek and to search out" (Ecc 1:13, 17; 7:25; 8:9, 16); "great searchings of heart" (Judg 5:15–16).; *Pondering and treasuring:* Mary "treasured up all these things, pondering them in her heart" (Luk 2:19, 51); "ponder in your own hearts on your beds" (Psa 4:4); "the meditation of my heart" (Psa 19:14; 49:3).; *Questioning and reasoning:* Mar 2:6, 8; Luk 3:15; 5:22; 9:47; 24:38.

17237.text: e. Willing, deciding, purposing, being moved: *Deciding:*; "Daniel resolved" (Dan 1:8); "Joash decided" (2Ch 24:4); "has determined this in his heart" (1Co 7:37); "Each one must give as he has decided in his heart" (2Co 9:7); "of my own will / accord" (Num 24:13; 16:28, lēv); "It is in my heart to make a covenant" (2Ch 29:10); "I had it in my heart to build a house" (1Ch 22:7; 28:2; 1Ki 8:17–18); *Being moved to give:* "everyone whose heart stirred him … and everyone whose spirit moved him" (Exo 35:21); also Exo 25:2; 35:5, 22, 26, 29; 36:2; 2Ki 12:4 ("the money that a man's heart prompts him to bring").; *Intention as depth:* "The purpose in a man's heart is like deep water, but a man of understanding will draw it out" (Pro 20:5); "the inward mind and heart of a man are deep" (Psa 64:6).

17238.text: f. Feeling: *Joy and gladness:* 1Ki 8:66; Pro 15:13, 15; 27:9, 11; Psa 4:7; 13:5; 16:9; 19:8; 28:7; 33:21; Zep 3:14; Joh 16:22.; *Merriment with wine:* Est 1:10; 2Sa 13:28; Rut 3:7; Judg 16:25; 19:6, 22.; *Sorrow and anguish:* Neh 2:2; Rom 9:2; 2Co 2:4; Joh 16:6; Psa 13:2; 55:4; Lam 1:20; 5:15.; *Fear and melting:* Gen 42:28; 1Sa 28:5; Deu 20:3, 8; Jos 7:5; Isa 7:2; 13:7; 21:4; 35:4; Jer 4:9; Nah 2:10.; *Courage:* Psa 27:14; 31:24; 2Sa 7:27; 17:10; Eze 22:14; Amo 2:16; Psa 76:5; plus the NT compounds "take heart" (Mat 9:2, 22; 14:27; Mar 6:50; 10:49; Joh 16:33; Act 23:11) and "lose heart" (Luk 18:1; 2Co 4:1, 16; Eph 3:13; Gal 6:9; 2Th 3:13).; *Desire:* "the desires of your heart" (Psa 37:4); "heart's desire" (Psa 21:2; 20:4; Rom 10:1).; *Love, attachment, contempt, hate:*; "the king's heart went out to Absalom" (2Sa 14:1); "my heart goes out to the commanders" (Judg 5:9); "your heart is not with me" (Judg 16:15); "I hold you in my heart" (Phili 1:7); "you are in our hearts, to die together and to live together" (2Co 7:3); "despised him in her heart" (2Sa 6:16); "You shall not hate your brother in your heart" (Lev 19:17); *Grief felt in the heart as physical pain:* "My anguish, my anguish! I writhe in pain! Oh the walls of my heart! My heart is beating wildly" (Jer 4:19); "My heart throbs" (Psa 38:10); "my heart is like wax; it is melted within my breast" (Psa 22:14).

17239.text: g. Moral character and orientation: *Qualities:* pure, upright, blameless, whole, perfect (1Ki 8:61; 15:14; Psa 24:4; 73:1; Mat 5:8; 2Ti 2:22); crooked, perverse, evil, deceitful, proud, haughty, stubborn (Pro 11:20; 17:20; 16:5; Jer 17:9; Jer 7:24 and the "stubbornness of their evil heart" series; Eze 28:2, 17; Obd 3).; *Direction:*; turns (1Ki 11:3–4, 9; Deu 29:18; 30:17), inclines (Psa 119:36, 112; 141:4; Jos 24:23; Judg 9:3), goes after (Eze 11:21; 20:16; 33:31; Job 31:7), is set on (Psa 62:10; Dan 11:28); is near or far (Isa 29:13; Mat 15:8; Mar 7:6); is "toward" someone (1Ch 29:18; 2Ch 16:9); "For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also" (Mat 6:21; Luk 12:34); *Whole vs divided:* "with all their heart / whole heart" (many verses; e.g. Psa 119:2, 10, 34, 58, 69, 145; 138:1; Jer 24:7; 29:13; 2Ch 15:15; 31:21); "not with a whole heart" (2Ch 25:2); "double heart" (Psa 12:2); "unite my heart to fear your name" (Psa 86:11); "one heart" (Jer 32:39; 2Ch 30:12; Eze 11:19); "purify your hearts, you double-minded" (Jam 4:8).

17241.text: i. The heart as a surface, container, store, soil: *Written on:*; "write them on the tablet of your heart" (Pro 3:3; 7:3); sin "engraved on the tablet of their heart" (Jer 17:1); "I will write it on their hearts" (Jer 31:33; Heb 8:10; 10:16); "tablets of human hearts" (2Co 3:3); "written on our hearts" (2Co 3:2); "the work of the law is written on their hearts" (Rom 2:15); *Stored in:*; "I have stored up your word in my heart" (Psa 119:11); "lay up these words … in your heart" (Deu 11:18; Job 22:22); "keep them within your heart" (Pro 4:21); "laid them up in their hearts" (Luk 1:66); "the good treasure of his heart" (Luk 6:45); *Things put in or taken in:*; "idols into their hearts" (Eze 14:3–7); "eternity into man's heart" (Ecc 3:11); "the law of his God is in his heart" (Psa 37:31; Isa 51:7); "the fear of me in their hearts" (Jer 32:40); "wisdom rests in the heart" (Pro 14:33); "wisdom will come into your heart" (Pro 2:10); *Soil:* "hold it fast in an honest and good heart, and bear fruit" (Luk 8:15); "what has been sown in his heart" snatched away (Mat 13:19; Luk 8:12).; *Vessel filled:* "Satan filled your heart" (Act 5:3); "sorrow has filled your heart" (Joh 16:6); "hearts full of evil" (Ecc 9:3); "hearts overflow with follies" (Psa 73:7).

17242.text: j. The heart's own "senses": fringe: "having the eyes of your hearts enlightened" (Eph 1:18); "God … has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge" (2Co 4:6); "until … the morning star rises in your hearts" (2Pe 1:19); "a veil lies over their hearts" (2Co 3:15).; fringe: "I slept, but my heart was awake" (Song 5:2); "Even in the night his heart does not rest" (Ecc 2:23).

17243.text: k. Heart states described through materials [Claude reading on the pattern; the images are the text's]: stone (Eze 11:19; 36:26; Job 41:24; 1Sa 25:37 "his heart died within him, and he became as a stone"); diamond (Zec 7:12); wax, water, melting (Psa 22:14; Jos 7:5; 2Sa 17:10); fat, unfeeling (Psa 119:70); "fattened your hearts" (Jam 5:5); oven (Hos 7:6); deep water (Pro 20:5); a stream of water in God's hand (Pro 21:1); grass struck down and withered (Psa 102:4); burning (Luk 24:32); a mirror: "As in water face reflects face, so the heart of man reflects the man" (Pro 27:19)

17244.text: l. The heart's opacity and privacy: "The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately sick; who can understand it?" (Jer 17:9); "the heart of kings is unsearchable" (Pro 25:3); "The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger shares its joy" (Pro 14:10); "he knows the secrets of the heart" (Psa 44:21); "the secrets of his heart are disclosed" (1Co 14:25); "disclose the purposes of the heart" (1Co 4:5); Only God knows it: 1Ki 8:39; 2Ch 6:30; 1Sa 16:7 ("man looks on the outward appearance, but the Lord looks on the heart"); Luk 16:15; Act 1:24 ("heart-knower"); Act 15:8; "who can say, 'I have made my heart pure'?" (Pro 20:9)

17245.text: m. Heart as the seat of self-judgment (conscience function in the OT): "David's heart struck him" (1Sa 24:5; 2Sa 24:10); "pangs of conscience" — ESV for *lēv* (1Sa 25:31); "Your heart knows that many times you yourself have cursed others" (Ecc 7:22); "my heart does not reproach me" (Job 27:6); NT: "whenever our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart … if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence" (1Jo 3:20–21)

17246.text: n. Heart and "mind": *ESV renders lēv as "mind":* 1Ki 3:9, 12; 4:29; 10:24; Pro 19:21; 28:26; Jer 14:14; 23:16; Lam 3:21; Neh 4:6; 6:8; 2Ki 6:11.; *Aramaic lēvav (H3825) is mostly "mind":* Dan 2:30; 4:16; 5:21; 7:4.; *Pairs in the text:* "test the heart and the mind" (Jer 11:20; 17:10; 20:12; Psa 26:2; 7:9; Rev 2:23); "hearts and … minds" (Phili 4:7); law "into their minds … on their hearts" / "on their hearts … on their minds" (Heb 8:10 / 10:16).; [lexical; verify] In several "heart and mind" pairs, the ESV "heart" may translate *kilyah* (kidneys) or the reverse. The CSV tags only the M47 word, so which English word carries the M47 tag varies (e.g. Jer 11:20, where the M47 tag sits on "mind").; fringe: a human heart/mind can be exchanged for a beast's and back: "let his mind be changed from a man's, and let a beast's mind be given to him" (Dan 4:16; 5:21); a beast is "given the mind of a man" (Dan 7:4).

17248.text: neck / throat (H5315N) | "the waters have come up to my neck" (Psa 69:1); "his neck was put in a collar of iron" (Psa 105:18)

17249.text: appetite / craving (H5315L) | "put a knife to your throat if you are given to appetite" (Pro 23:2) — fringe: throat and appetite side by side; "All the toil of man is for his mouth, yet his appetite is not satisfied" (Ecc 6:7); "a worker's appetite works for him; his mouth urges him on" (Pro 16:26); "Sheol has enlarged its appetite and opened its mouth" (Isa 5:14) — fringe: *nephesh* given to Sheol

17254.text: living creature (H5315K) | Gen 1:20–24; "the man became a living creature" (Gen 2:7)

17256.text: b. What the soul characteristically does: *Needs and seeks:* thirsts, longs, pants, faints (Psa 107:5; 119:81; Isa 26:8–9), waits (Psa 33:20; 62:1, 5; 130:5–6), hopes (Lam 3:24), clings (Psa 63:8; 119:25 "clings to the dust").; *Suffers:*; bitter (1Sa 1:10; 22:2; 30:6; Job 3:20; 7:11; 10:1; 21:25; 27:2; Isa 38:15; Eze 27:31); cast down, in turmoil (Psa 42:5, 6, 11; 43:5); bowed down (Psa 44:25; 57:6; Lam 3:20); poured out (1Sa 1:15; Job 30:16; Psa 42:4; Isa 53:12 "poured out his soul to death"); refuses comfort (Psa 77:2); is troubled (Psa 6:3; Joh 12:27); "very sorrowful, even to death" (Mat 26:38; Mar 14:34); "my soul is bereft of peace; I have forgotten what happiness is" (Lam 3:17); "vexed to death" (Judg 16:16); *Responds with joy and worship:* rejoices and exults (Isa 61:10; Psa 35:9); boasts in the Lord (Psa 34:2); blesses the Lord (Psa 103:1–2, 22; 104:1, 35; 146:1); "My soul magnifies the Lord" (Luk 1:46); keeps testimonies (Psa 119:129, 167); knows (Psa 139:14).; *Loves and hates:* "the soul of Jonathan was knit to the soul of David" (1Sa 18:1); "his soul hates the wicked" (Psa 11:5); "soul abhors" (Lev 26:15, 43); "malice of soul" (Eze 25:6, 15).; *Is satisfied or not:* Psa 63:5; 107:9; Jer 31:14, 25; Ecc 6:3; Pro 13:4.; *Is lifted up:* "To you, O Lord, I lift up my soul" (Psa 25:1; 86:4; 143:8); contrast "who does not lift up his soul to what is false" (Psa 24:4).; *Is addressed by its owner* — fringe, but many verses: "Why are you cast down, O my soul?" (Psa 42:5, 11; 43:5); "Bless the Lord, O my soul" (Psa 103:1); "Return, O my soul, to your rest" (Psa 116:7); "For God alone, O my soul, wait in silence" (Psa 62:5); "I have calmed and quieted my soul" (Psa 131:2); "March on, my soul, with might!" (Judg 5:21); The rich fool: "I will say to my soul, 'Soul, … relax, eat, drink, be merry'" (Luk 12:19); [Claude reading] The soul is something a person can stand beside, speak to, quiet and command. There is an "I" that addresses "my soul".

17257.text: c. What is done to the soul: *Hunted, pursued, torn:* Eze 13:18–20 ("hunt the souls like birds"); Psa 7:2, 5; 143:3; 57:4.; *Delivered, redeemed, ransomed, kept:* Psa 116:4, 8; 49:15; 55:18; 86:13; 1Ki 1:29; Psa 25:20; 121:7.; *Restored, revived:* "He restores my soul" (Psa 23:3); "The law of the Lord is perfect, reviving the soul" (Psa 19:7).; *Nourished by words:*; "Gracious words … sweetness to the soul and health to the body" (Pro 16:24); "Like cold water to a thirsty soul, so is good news" (Pro 25:25); a faithful messenger "refreshes the soul" (Pro 25:13); wisdom "life for your soul" (Pro 3:22; 24:14); *NT:*; "passions of the flesh, which wage war against your soul" (1Pe 2:11); "Having purified your souls by your obedience to the truth" (1Pe 1:22); "the implanted word, which is able to save your souls" (Jam 1:21); "anchor of the soul" (Heb 6:19); "they entice unsteady souls" (2Pe 2:14); "unsettling your minds / poisoned their minds" (psychē, Act 15:24; 14:2)

17259.text: a. One word: wind, breath, spirit, Spirit, spirits, side, temper: *Wind:* storms, the east wind, the four winds (e.g. Exo 14:21; 1Ki 19:11; Jon 1:4; Psa 1:4).; *Breath:* "the breath of life" (Gen 7:22); "put breath in you, and you shall live" (Eze 37:5–10).; *A person's spirit:* troubled, revived, broken, lowly (below).; *God's Spirit:* rushing upon, filling, indwelling (below).; *Other spirits:* lying (1Ki 22:21–23), harmful (1Sa 16:14–23), unclean (Mar 1–9; Luk 4–11), deceitful (1Ti 4:1).; *"Side" of the compass* (H7307I; 1Ch 9:24; Eze 42:16–20) — fringe: *wind* = *direction*.; *Temper* (H7307J): "hasty temper" (Pro 14:29); "cool spirit" (Pro 17:27); "A fool gives full vent to his spirit" (Pro 29:11); "A man without self-control is like a city broken into and left without walls" (Pro 25:28) — fringe: self-control = governing one's *rûaḥ*; lacking it = a city without walls.; fringe: "the Lord God walking in the garden in the cool [rûaḥ] of the day" (Gen 3:8).

17260.text: b. The human spirit: *Troubled, anxious:* Gen 41:8; Dan 2:1, 3; 7:15 ("my spirit within me was anxious, and the visions of my head alarmed me"); Joh 13:21; 2Co 2:13.; *Revived:*; after eating ("his spirit revived" 1Sa 30:12); after drinking ("his spirit returned, and he revived" Judg 15:19); on good news (Gen 45:27); *Broken, crushed:* Exo 6:9 ("broken spirit and harsh slavery"); Pro 15:4, 13; 17:22; 18:14 ("A man's spirit will endure sickness, but a crushed spirit who can bear?"); Job 17:1; Psa 34:18; 51:17.; *Faint, failing:* Psa 77:3; 142:3; 143:4, 7; Isa 57:16; 61:3.; *Lowly, contrite vs proud, haughty:* Isa 57:15; 66:2; Pro 16:18–19; 29:23; Ecc 7:8; Mat 5:3 ("poor in spirit").; *Governed or ungoverned:* "he who rules his spirit than he who takes a city" (Pro 16:32); "Be not quick in your spirit to become angry" (Ecc 7:9).; *Weighed by God:* "the Lord weighs the spirit" (Pro 16:2).; *Knowing and understanding:*; "it is the spirit in man, the breath of the Almighty, that makes him understand" (Job 32:8); "out of my understanding a spirit answers me" (Job 20:3); "the spirit within me constrains me" (Job 32:18); "who knows a person's thoughts except the spirit of that person, which is in him?" (1Co 2:11) — [Claude reading] the spirit as the person's self-knowledge.; *Distinct from "mind" (nous) in prayer:* "my spirit prays but my mind is unfruitful … I will pray with my spirit, but I will pray with my mind also" (1Co 14:14–15); "be renewed in the spirit of your minds" (Eph 4:23).; *Jesus' spirit:* "perceiving in his spirit" (Mar 2:8); "sighed deeply in his spirit" (Mar 8:12); "deeply moved in his spirit" (Joh 11:33); "troubled in his spirit" (Joh 13:21); "yielded up his spirit" (Mat 27:50; Joh 19:30; Luk 23:46).; *Paul's spirit:* "his spirit was provoked within him" (Act 17:16); "my spirit was not at rest" (2Co 2:13); "refreshed my spirit" (1Co 16:18); "I serve with my spirit" (Rom 1:9).; *Fervent:* "fervent in spirit" (Rom 12:11; Act 18:25); "grew and became strong in spirit" (Luk 1:80).; *Stirred by God:*; "the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus" (2Ch 36:22; Ezr 1:1); "everyone whose spirit God had stirred" (Ezr 1:5); the spirit of Zerubbabel (Hag 1:14); of Pul (1Ch 5:26); of the Medes (Jer 51:11); *Hardened by God:* "the Lord your God hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate" (Deu 2:30).

17263.text: d. God's Spirit acting on and in the inner seat: *Comes upon, rushes upon, clothes:* Judg 3:10; 6:34; 14:6, 19; 15:14; 1Sa 10:6, 10 ("be turned into another man"); 16:13; 1Ch 12:18; 2Ch 24:20.; *Fills with ability:* "filled him with the Spirit of God, with ability and intelligence, with knowledge and all craftsmanship" (Exo 31:3; 35:31).; *Enters and sets on feet:* Eze 2:2; 3:24.; *Put within → changed conduct:* "I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes" (Eze 36:27; 37:14).; *Dwells in:* Rom 8:9, 11; 1Co 3:16; "your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you" (1Co 6:19); 2Ti 1:14; Jam 4:5 ("the spirit that he has made to dwell in us").; *Bears witness with our spirit:* Rom 8:16.; *Placed in the heart:* "given his Spirit in our hearts" (2Co 1:22); "sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, 'Abba! Father!'" (Gal 4:6).; *Pours love into hearts:* Rom 5:5.; *Writes on hearts:* 2Co 3:3.; *Strengthens the inner being:* Eph 3:16.; *Intercedes:* Rom 8:26–27 ("he who searches hearts knows what is the mind of the Spirit").; *Can be grieved, resisted, lied to, quenched:* Isa 63:10; Eph 4:30; Act 7:51 ("uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit"); Act 5:3; 1Th 5:19.; *Can depart or be taken:* 1Sa 16:14; Psa 51:11.; *In the nostrils / made me:* "as long as my breath is in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils" (Job 27:3); "The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life" (Job 33:4).; *Formed within:* "who … formed the spirit of man within him" (Zec 12:1); "gives breath to the people … and spirit to those who walk in it" (Isa 42:5).

17264.text: e. Wind and breath in relation to the inner being — explicitly retained per the researcher: *Breath = life in flesh:*; "all flesh in which is the breath of life" (Gen 6:17; 7:15, 22); "sinews … flesh … skin … But there was no breath in them" → "breath came into them, and they lived" (Eze 37:6–10); "When you take away their breath, they die and return to their dust" (Psa 104:29); *Breath and thought:* "When his breath departs, he returns to the earth; on that very day his plans perish" (Psa 146:4). Link to the thought vocabulary (see brief §5).; *Breath as frailty:* "Remember that my life is a breath" (Job 7:7); "They all have the same breath, and man has no advantage over the beasts" (Ecc 3:19); "He remembered that they were but flesh, a wind that passes and comes not again" (Psa 78:39).; *No breath = no inner life:* idols have "no breath in them" (Jer 10:14; 51:17; Hab 2:19; Psa 135:17). fringe: "there was no more breath in her" = the queen of Sheba overwhelmed (1Ki 10:5; 2Ch 9:4).; *Wind as the emptiness of inner striving* (Ecclesiastes): "I applied my heart to know wisdom … this also is but a striving after wind" (Ecc 1:17); the same in 1:14; 2:11, 17, 26; 4:4, 6, 16; 5:16; "Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the appetite: this also is vanity and a striving after wind" (Ecc 6:9) — appetite (nephesh) + wind; *Wind as empty words:*; "windy knowledge … fill his belly with the east wind" (Job 15:2); "windy words" (Job 16:3); "the speech of a despairing man is wind" (Job 6:26); "the words of your mouth be a great wind" (Job 8:2); "The prophets will become wind; the word is not in them" (Jer 5:13); "utter wind and lies" (Mic 2:11); *Wind as empty outcome:* "we have given birth to wind" (Isa 26:18); "Whoever troubles his own household will inherit the wind" (Pro 11:29); "sow the wind, and … reap the whirlwind" (Hos 8:7); "Ephraim feeds on the wind" (Hos 12:1).; *Wind as the image for a shaken heart:* "the heart of Ahaz and the heart of his people shook as the trees of the forest shake before the wind" (Isa 7:2).; *Wind and lust:* "a wild donkey … in her heat sniffing the wind! Who can restrain her lust?" (Jer 2:24); "to restrain her is to restrain the wind" (Pro 27:16).

17265.text: e. Wind and breath in relation to the inner being — explicitly retained per the researcher: *Wind as the image of Spirit-birth:* "The wind blows where it wishes … So it is with everyone who is born of the Spirit" (Joh 3:8). Here the text itself uses wind to picture the Spirit's action on a person.

17266.text: a. Hebrew flesh: the whole visible, related, mortal person: *Body and meat:* the purity law (Lev 13–16), sacrifices, "meat" in the wilderness (Num 11) and in cooking.; *Kin:*; "we are your bone and flesh" (2Sa 5:1; Gen 29:14); "he is our brother, our own flesh" (Gen 37:27); "not to hide yourself from your own flesh" (Isa 58:7); "close relative" (Lev 18:6; 25:49, H7607); "one flesh" (Gen 2:24; Mat 19:5–6; Mar 10:8; Eph 5:31); *"All flesh" = every living being / humankind:* Gen 6:12–13; Isa 40:5–6 ("All flesh is grass"); Jer 32:27 ("the God of all flesh"); "the God of the spirits of all flesh" (Num 16:22; 27:16).; *Frailty in contrast to God:*; "What can flesh do to me?" (Psa 56:4); "an arm of flesh" (2Ch 32:8); "Cursed is the man who trusts in man and makes flesh his strength, whose heart turns away from the Lord" (Jer 17:5); "their horses are flesh, and not spirit" (Isa 31:3); "My Spirit shall not abide in man forever, for he is flesh" (Gen 6:3); *Flesh responding to the inner seat:*; "My flesh trembles for fear of you" (Psa 119:120); "shuddering seizes my flesh" (Job 21:6); "the hair of my flesh stood up" when a spirit glided past (Job 4:15) — spirit → flesh; "my soul thirsts for you; my flesh faints for you" (Psa 63:1); "my heart and flesh sing for joy" (Psa 84:2); "my heart is glad … my flesh also dwells secure" (Psa 16:9; Act 2:26); "My flesh and my heart may fail" (Psa 73:26); "A tranquil heart gives life to the flesh" (Pro 14:30); "they are life to those who find them, and healing to all their flesh" (Pro 4:22); "There is no soundness in my flesh because of your indignation; there is no health in my bones because of my sin" (Psa 38:3); "much study is a weariness of the flesh" (Ecc 12:12); "Ahab … put sackcloth on his flesh" (1Ki 21:27); *Heart of flesh vs heart of stone:* "I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh" (Eze 11:19; 36:26). Here *flesh* is the good state of the heart: responsive, living.; *Life is in the blood of the flesh:* "the life of the flesh is in the blood" (Lev 17:11, 14; Gen 9:4; Deu 12:23).

17268.text: 2.5 Conscience — *syneidēsis* (G4893, NT only): *Bears witness:* "their conscience also bears witness, and their conflicting thoughts accuse or even excuse them" (Rom 2:15); "my conscience bears me witness in the Holy Spirit" (Rom 9:1); "the testimony of our conscience" (2Co 1:12).; *Good, clear:* Act 23:1; 24:16; 1Ti 1:5, 19; 3:9; 2Ti 1:3; Heb 13:18; 1Pe 3:16.; *Weak, defiled, wounded:* 1Co 8:7, 10, 12. *Seared:* 1Ti 4:2. *Evil:* Heb 10:22.; *Defiled together with the mind:* "both their minds and their consciences are defiled" (Tit 1:15).; *Purified:* "the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself … [will] purify our conscience from dead works" (Heb 9:14); gifts and sacrifices "cannot perfect the conscience" (Heb 9:9); "consciousness of sins" (Heb 10:2).; *Other people's conscience:* "not your conscience, but his" (1Co 10:29); "commend ourselves to everyone's conscience" (2Co 4:2); "known also to your conscience" (2Co 5:11); "for the sake of conscience" (Rom 13:5; 1Co 10:25–28).; *Baptism as "an appeal to God for a good conscience"*, not removal of dirt from the body (1Pe 3:21).; fringe: "mindful of God" (1Pe 2:19) and "consciousness" (Heb 10:2) are tagged G4893. The word covers *awareness* as well as moral judgment [Claude reading].

17269.text: 2.6 Bosom / embrace — *ḥêq* (H2436G) ◆ mostly fringe, but relevant: *Holding loved ones:* in her arms, at her breast, on her lap (1Ki 3:20; 17:19; Rut 4:16); "carry them in your bosom, as a nurse carries a nursing child" (Num 11:12); "he will carry them in his bosom" (Isa 40:11); "the wife you embrace" (Deu 13:6; 28:54, 56).; *As an inner seat:*; "anger lodges in the heart [bosom] of fools" (Ecc 7:9); "how I bear in my heart [bosom] the insults of all the many nations" (Psa 89:50); "My heart faints within me!" (Job 19:27; tagged on "within"); "I prayed with head bowed on my chest" (Psa 35:13); *Life poured out on the bosom:* "their life is poured out on their mothers' bosom" (Lam 2:12).; [Claude reading] The bosom is where one holds *others* and where one holds *feelings* (anger, insults). The same place carries both.

17270.text: 3.1 Parallel and interchangeable (poetic pairing): *Heart // spirit:*; "Create in me a clean heart … renew a right spirit within me" (Psa 51:10); "a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart" (Psa 51:17); "brokenhearted … crushed in spirit" (Psa 34:18); "revive the spirit of the lowly … the heart of the contrite" (Isa 57:15); "my spirit faints within me; my heart within me is appalled" (Psa 143:4); "Every heart will melt … every spirit will faint" (Eze 21:7); "heart was not steadfast … spirit was not faithful" (Psa 78:8); "meditate in my heart … my spirit made a diligent search" (Psa 77:6); "whose heart stirred him … whose spirit moved him" (Exo 35:21); "gladness of heart … pain of heart … breaking of spirit" (Isa 65:14); Aramaic: "his heart was lifted up and his spirit was hardened" (Dan 5:20); *Soul // spirit:*; "My soul yearns for you in the night; my spirit within me earnestly seeks you" (Isa 26:9); "the anguish of my spirit … the bitterness of my soul" (Job 7:11); Hannah: "troubled in spirit … pouring out my soul" (1Sa 1:15); "My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior" (Luk 1:46–47); *Heart // soul:*; "wisdom will come into your heart, and knowledge will be pleasant to your soul" (Pro 2:10); "take counsel in my soul and have sorrow in my heart" (Psa 13:2); "he who weighs the heart … he who keeps watch over your soul" (Pro 24:12); English-only parallels, not supported by the tags [verify]: "When the cares of my heart are many, your consolations cheer my soul" (Psa 94:19). Only *nephesh* is tagged; the ESV "heart" there is not an M47 word.; "When my soul was embittered, when I was pricked in heart" (Psa 73:21). The tag is H3824 on "soul". [lexical] The Hebrew is probably *lēvāv* // kidneys, with the ESV swapping them.; *Heart // mind:* "a whole heart … a willing mind" (1Ch 28:9, where "mind" = nephesh); "whole heart … single mind" (1Ch 12:38); Heb 8:10 vs 10:16 (heart and mind swap places).; *Cross-rendering in the ESV:*; nephesh → "heart" (Exo 23:9; Jer 15:1; Pro 19:18; 29:17; Lev 26:16; 1Sa 2:33; 2Sa 3:21; 1Sa 23:20; Psa 35:25); nephesh → "spirit" (Lam 1:16); nephesh → "mind" (1Sa 2:35; 1Ch 28:9); psychē → "heart / heartily / fainthearted" (Eph 6:6; Col 3:23; Heb 12:3) and → "minds" (Act 14:2; 15:24); rûaḥ → "mind" (1Ch 28:12; Eze 11:5; 20:32)

17271.text: 3.1 Parallel and interchangeable (poetic pairing): [Claude reading] The translators move between heart, soul, spirit and mind when rendering the same Hebrew or Greek word. That movement is itself evidence that the words' ranges overlap.

17272.text: 3.2 Totality and wholeness formulas: *Heart and soul (and might):*; "with all your heart and with all your soul (and with all your might)" (Deu 4:29; 6:5; 10:12; 11:13; 13:3; 26:16; 30:2, 6, 10; Jos 22:5; 1Ki 2:4; 8:48; 2Ki 23:3, 25; 2Ch 6:38; 15:12; 34:31; Jer 32:41 — said of God); "you know in your hearts and souls" (Jos 23:14); "lay up these words … in your heart and in your soul" (Deu 11:18); "keep your soul diligently, lest … they depart from your heart" (Deu 4:9); "I am with you heart and soul" (1Sa 14:7, ESV idiom; only *lēvāv* is tagged); "one heart and soul" (Act 4:32); *NT expansion — heart, soul, mind, strength:* Mat 22:37; Mar 12:30; Luk 10:27; "heart … understanding … strength" (Mar 12:33).; *Whole person with an outer term added:*; "spirit and soul and body" (1Th 5:23); "soul and body" (Isa 10:18; Mat 10:28; Psa 31:9; Pro 16:24); "heart and flesh" (Psa 73:26; 84:2; Eze 44:7, 9); "body and spirit" (1Co 7:34; 2Co 7:1); "vexation from your heart … pain from your body" (Ecc 11:10); [Claude reading] Wholeness is expressed by *adding* terms, not by defining parts. The pairs work as merisms: the whole person seen from two or three sides at once.

17273.text: 3.3 Unity and division: *Unity:*; "unite my heart" (Psa 86:11); "one heart" (Jer 32:39; Eze 11:19; 2Ch 30:12); "one heart and soul" (Act 4:32); "one spirit, with one mind" (Phili 1:27); "one flesh" (Gen 2:24); "he who is joined to the Lord becomes one spirit with him" (1Co 6:17); *Division:*; "double heart" (Psa 12:2); "double-minded" (Jam 4:8); "his heart was not wholly true" (1Ki 11:4; 15:3); "not with a whole heart" (2Ch 25:2); "The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak" (Mat 26:41); "the desires of the flesh are against the Spirit … to keep you from doing the things you want to do" (Gal 5:17); [Claude reading] Division *within* a person is described as a split heart or as spirit against flesh. Union *between* persons uses the same terms (one heart, one soul, one flesh, one spirit).

17274.text: 3.4 Distinction — where the text separates the components: *Division of soul and spirit (Heb 4:12):* "piercing to the division of soul and of spirit, of joints and of marrow, and discerning the thoughts and intentions of the heart." [Claude reading] Soul and spirit are close enough that only the word of God can separate them, just as joints and marrow are adjacent parts of the body. The heart is where the *thoughts and intentions* are, and they are *discerned* there.; *Living soul vs life-giving spirit:* "The first man Adam became a living being [psychē]; the last Adam became a life-giving spirit" (1Co 15:45; cf. Gen 2:7).; *Spirit vs mind:* 1Co 14:14–15 (above).; *Spirit vs flesh (as kind):*; "a spirit does not have flesh and bones" (Luk 24:39); "horses are flesh, and not spirit" (Isa 31:3); "That which is born of the flesh is flesh, and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit" (Joh 3:6); "the flesh is no help at all" (Joh 6:63); "put to death in the flesh but made alive in the spirit" (1Pe 3:18; 4:6); "the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved" (1Co 5:5); *Soul vs body:* "cannot kill the soul" (Mat 10:28).; *Spirit vs body in place:* "absent in body, … present in spirit" (1Co 5:3–4; Col 2:5). fringe [Claude reading]: the spirit can be "with" people where the body is not.; *Inner vs outer:*; "Though our outer self is wasting away, our inner self is being renewed day by day" (2Co 4:16, with "lose heart"); "a Jew is one inwardly, and circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit" (Rom 2:29); "the hidden person of the heart with the imperishable beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit" (1Pe 3:4); "man looks on the outward appearance, but the Lord looks on the heart" (1Sa 16:7); "what is in the heart" vs "outward appearance" (2Co 5:12); *Food and the heart:* "since it enters not his heart but his stomach, and is expelled" (Mar 7:19). The text draws a boundary: food goes to the stomach, not the heart. But see §3.6, where food *does* strengthen the heart.

17275.text: 3.5 Opposition: *Flesh vs Spirit* (Paul): Gal 3:3; 4:29; 5:16–17; 6:8; Rom 8:4–9, 13; Phili 3:3.; *Flesh's passions vs soul:* "passions of the flesh, which wage war against your soul" (1Pe 2:11).; *Mind vs flesh:* Rom 7:25.; *Hebrew background:*; "He remembered that they were but flesh" (Psa 78:39); "My Spirit shall not abide in man forever, for he is flesh" (Gen 6:3); trusting flesh ↔ heart turning from the Lord (Jer 17:5); [Claude reading] In the OT verses read here, flesh is frail, not hostile. The hostility of flesh to Spirit is NT-specific in this dataset. Even in the NT, neutral flesh remains (one flesh, Word became flesh, "the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith" Gal 2:20).

17276.text: 3.6 Cause and effect between inner seat, body and senses: *Heart → spirit:* "by sorrow of heart the spirit is crushed" (Pro 15:13).; *Heart / spirit → body, face, bones:*; "A glad heart makes a cheerful face" (Pro 15:13); "A tranquil heart gives life to the flesh, but envy makes the bones rot" (Pro 14:30); "A joyful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones" (Pro 17:22); "a trembling heart and failing eyes and a languishing soul" (Deu 28:65); "My heart throbs; my strength fails me, and the light of my eyes — it also has gone" (Psa 38:10); "Every heart will melt, and all hands will be feeble; every spirit will faint, and all knees will be weak as water" (Eze 21:7); "Hearts melt and knees tremble; anguish is in all loins; all faces grow pale" (Nah 2:10); "My heart is struck down like grass … I forget to eat my bread" (Psa 102:4); "My heart is broken within me; all my bones shake" (Jer 23:9); "your heart shall rejoice; your bones shall flourish like the grass" (Isa 66:14); "For this our heart has become sick, for these things our eyes have grown dim" (Lam 5:17); "my stomach churns; my heart is wrung within me" (Lam 1:20); *Body / face / senses → heart:*; "by sadness of face the heart is made glad" (Ecc 7:3); "The light of the eyes rejoices the heart, and good news refreshes the bones" (Pro 15:30); "my heart has gone after my eyes" (Job 31:7); "not to follow after your own heart and your own eyes" (Num 15:39); "everyone who looks at a woman with lustful intent has already committed adultery with her in his heart" (Mat 5:28); *Food and drink → heart / spirit / soul:*; "Strengthen your heart with a morsel of bread" (Judg 19:5, 8); "wine to gladden the heart of man … bread to strengthen man's heart" (Psa 104:15); "satisfying your hearts with food and gladness" (Act 14:17); "when he had eaten, his spirit revived" (1Sa 30:12); "when he drank, his spirit returned" (Judg 15:19); "when the wine had gone out of Nabal … his heart died within him, and he became as a stone" (1Sa 25:37); "it is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace, not by foods" (Heb 13:9); "Oil and perfume make the heart glad" (Pro 27:9); *Fasting afflicts the soul:* Psa 35:13 ("I afflicted myself [nephesh] with fasting"); Psa 69:10; Isa 58:3, 5; the Day of Atonement "afflict yourselves" (Lev 16:29–31; 23:27–32; Num 29:7).

17277.text: 3.6 Cause and effect between inner seat, body and senses: *Appetite (soul) and heart:* "They tested God in their heart by demanding the food they craved" (Psa 78:18); the fool's heart "busy with iniquity … to leave the craving of the hungry unsatisfied" (Isa 32:6); "you crave meat" (Deu 12:20).; *Heart → mouth, hands, feet, deeds:* §2.1h. Also: "clean hands and a pure heart" (Psa 24:4); "Let us lift up our hearts and hands to God" (Lam 3:41); "a heart that devises wicked plans, feet that make haste to run to evil" (Pro 6:18); "The heart of man plans his way, but the Lord establishes his steps" (Pro 16:9); "The law of his God is in his heart; his steps do not slip" (Psa 37:31); *Heart ↔ ears / hearing* — link to the brief's hearing question: "hear with their ears, and understand with their hearts" (Isa 6:10; Mat 13:15; Act 28:27); "making your ear attentive to wisdom and inclining your heart to understanding" (Pro 2:2); "Incline your ear … apply your heart" (Pro 22:17; 23:12); "receive in your heart, and hear with your ears" (Eze 3:10); "hear with your ears … set your heart upon all that I shall show you" (Eze 40:4); "uncircumcised in heart and ears" (Act 7:51); "The Lord opened her heart to pay attention" (Act 16:14); "They made their hearts diamond-hard lest they should hear the law" (Zec 7:12); "Incline your ear, and come to me; hear, that your soul may live" (Isa 55:3) — soul + hearing; "Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts" (Heb 3:7–8, 15; 4:7; Psa 95:8); [Claude reading] Hearing and heart are joined repeatedly: the ear receives, the heart understands or refuses. Hardness of heart and failure to hear go together.

17278.text: 3.7 Containment — what is placed "in" what: *In the heart:*; law, words, commandments (Deu 6:6; Psa 37:31; 119:11; Jer 31:33); wisdom (Pro 2:10; 14:33); fear of God (Jer 32:40); eternity (Ecc 3:11); idols (Eze 14:3); deceit (Pro 12:20); folly (Pro 22:15); anger (Ecc 7:9); the Spirit (2Co 1:22; Gal 4:6); Christ "may dwell in your hearts through faith" (Eph 3:17); "the peace of Christ rule in your hearts" (Col 3:15); "the word of Christ dwell in you richly … thankfulness in your hearts" (Col 3:16); God's love "poured into our hearts" (Rom 5:5); what "the devil had already put into the heart of Judas" (Joh 13:2); what "God has put into their hearts" (Rev 17:17; Neh 2:12; 7:5; Ezr 7:27; 2Co 8:16); *Within me:* spirit (Psa 143:4; Isa 26:9; Job 32:18; Dan 7:15); soul (Psa 42:5–6; 131:2); heart (Psa 22:14; 39:3; 109:22; Jer 8:18; 23:9; Lam 1:20; Hos 11:8).; *Spirit and heart inside flesh:* "I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh" (Eze 36:26); "put breath in you" (Eze 37:6).; *Spirit and body:* "your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you" (1Co 6:19); "if the Spirit … dwells in you, he … will also give life to your mortal bodies" (Rom 8:11).; [Claude reading] The heart is the innermost *location* in the text's picture. Soul-states, spirit, God's Spirit, words, law and dispositions are placed "in" it. Spirit and soul are also spoken of as "within me", but they are less often described as containers.

17279.text: 3.8 The inner seat shared or joined between persons ◆ fringe cluster: *Soul to soul:*; "the soul of Jonathan was knit to the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul" (1Sa 18:1, 3; 20:17); "your friend who is as your own soul" (Deu 13:6, with "the wife you embrace"); "his life is bound up in the boy's life" (Gen 44:30); *Heart to heart:* "my heart will be joined to you" (1Ch 12:17); "Is your heart true to my heart as mine is to yours?" (2Ki 10:15); "you are in our hearts, to die together and to live together" (2Co 7:3); "I hold you in my heart" (Phili 1:7); "in person not in heart" (1Th 2:17).; *Shared across a group:* "one heart and soul" (Act 4:32); "one spirit, with one mind" (Phili 1:27); "Did we not act in the same spirit?" (2Co 12:18).; *Transferred between persons:* "a double portion of your spirit" (2Ki 2:9, 15); "take some of the Spirit that is on you and put it on them" (Num 11:17, 25); "in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children" (Luk 1:17; Mal 4:6).; *Captured or stolen by others:* "Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel" (2Sa 15:6); "his wives turned away his heart" (1Ki 11:3); "he swayed the heart of all the men of Judah as one man" (2Sa 19:14).; *Known from shared experience:* "You know the heart [nephesh] of a sojourner, for you were sojourners" (Exo 23:9).; *With a spouse:* "guard yourselves in your spirit, and let none of you be faithless to the wife of your youth" (Mal 2:15–16); "one flesh" (Gen 2:24).; [Claude reading] The inner seat is not depicted as sealed inside the individual. It can be knit to, joined with, held within, carried in, stolen by, or shared with another person. It can also be passed from one person to another (spirit).

17280.text: 3.9 The boundary of death — where the components come apart: *Soul departs:* "as her soul was departing" (Gen 35:18); soul to Sheol, pit, silence (§2.2d).; *Spirit and breath return to God:*; "the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it" (Ecc 12:7); "Who knows whether the spirit of man goes upward and the spirit of the beast goes down into the earth?" (Ecc 3:21); "When you take away their breath, they die and return to their dust" (Psa 104:29); "Into your hand I commit my spirit" (Psa 31:5; Luk 23:46; Act 7:59); "No man has power to retain the spirit" (Ecc 8:8); *Return to life:*; "her spirit returned, and she got up" (Luk 8:55); "the life of the child came into him again, and he revived" (1Ki 17:21–22), with "the flesh of the child became warm" (2Ki 4:34); "a breath of life from God entered them" (Rev 11:11); Ezekiel 37: flesh, sinews, skin → breath → life; *Life in the blood:* "the life [nephesh] of the flesh is in the blood" (Lev 17:11, 14; Gen 9:4–5; Deu 12:23).; *Body without spirit:* "the body apart from the spirit is dead" (Jam 2:26).; *Dead body = nephesh:* H5315M (Num 19:11, 13).; *Beyond death:* "the spirits of the righteous made perfect" (Heb 12:23); "the spirits in prison" (1Pe 3:19); "the souls … under the altar" (Rev 6:9).; *Plans perish when breath departs:* Psa 146:4.; [Claude reading] Death is where the text most clearly *separates* the terms: flesh/dust goes to the earth; spirit/breath goes to God; soul goes to Sheol, or is delivered; the blood carries the life; In ordinary life the same terms overlap and stand in for one another.

17281.text: 3.10 God, animals and things — the vocabulary is not limited to humans ◆ fringe: *God has a heart:* grieved (Gen 6:6); speaks in it (Gen 8:21); "a man after my own heart" (1Sa 13:14; Act 13:22); "My heart recoils within me; my compassion grows warm and tender" (Hos 11:8); "he does not afflict from his heart" (Lam 3:33); "my eyes and my heart will be there" (1Ki 9:3); "the intents of his heart" (Jer 23:20); "with all my heart and all my soul" (Jer 32:41).; *God has a soul:* "my soul hates" (Isa 1:14); "my soul delights" (Isa 42:1; Mat 12:18); "my soul shall not abhor you" (Lev 26:11); "Does your soul loathe Zion?" (Jer 14:19); "my soul has no pleasure in him" (Heb 10:38); "The Lord God has sworn by himself [nephesh]" (Amo 6:8; Jer 51:14); "shall I not avenge myself [nephesh]" (Jer 5:9, 29; 9:9).; *God's spirit and breath:* "the breath of his mouth" (Psa 33:6); "the breath of his lips" (Isa 11:4); "God is spirit" (Joh 4:24).; *Animals:*; "living creatures" (nephesh, Gen 1); "They all have the same breath" (Ecc 3:19); "the spirit of the beast" (Ecc 3:21); a beast's mind given to a man (Dan 4:16); "the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels" (Eze 1:20–21; 10:17); "all flesh" includes animals (Gen 6–9); *Places and things:* heart of the sea, earth and heaven (§2.1a); Sheol's appetite (Isa 5:14); idols with no breath (§2.3e).

17282.text: 4. Fringe observations collected (quick list): Heart = "midst" of sea, heaven, earth; the inner seat named as the *middle* (§2.1a).; Aaron carries the tribes "on his heart" before the Lord (Exo 28:29–30).; "I slept, but my heart was awake" (Song 5:2).; "Eyes of your hearts" (Eph 1:18); morning star rising in hearts (2Pe 1:19); a veil over hearts (2Co 3:15).; "Walls of my heart" (Jer 4:19); "tear open their breast" (Hos 13:8); a man without self-control = "a city … without walls" (Pro 25:28, rûaḥ). The inner seat is imaged as an enclosure.; Nabal's heart "died within him, and he became as a stone" after the wine left (1Sa 25:37).; Nephesh = neck/throat (Psa 69:1; 105:18) and = corpse (Num 19:11).; Knife to the throat "if you are given to appetite" (Pro 23:2).; Sheol's "appetite" and "mouth" (Isa 5:14).; "Perfume boxes" tagged nephesh (Isa 3:20).; A millstone in pledge = "a life in pledge" (Deu 24:6).; The soul addressed by its owner (Psa 42; 103; 116:7; 131:2; Luk 12:19).; rûaḥ = compass *side* (1Ch 9:24; Eze 42:16–20).; rûaḥ = "cool" of the day when God walked in the garden (Gen 3:8).; Dispositions as "spirits" that come upon a person: jealousy, whoredom, confusion, deep sleep, stupor, skill, grace (§2.3c).; Spirits causing muteness or a bent back (Mar 9:17; Luk 13:11).; "A spirit glided past my face; the hair of my flesh stood up" (Job 4:15).; "Present in spirit" though absent in body (1Co 5:3; Col 2:5).; Spirit of Elijah on Elisha; Moses' Spirit shared with the elders (2Ki 2; Num 11).; Queen of Sheba: "there was no more breath in her" (1Ki 10:5).; Man's heart/mind exchanged for a beast's (Dan 4:16; 5:21; 7:4).; "The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger shares its joy" (Pro 14:10) — the privacy of the inner seat.; "As in water face reflects face, so the heart of man reflects the man" (Pro 27:19).; "He has put eternity into man's heart" (Ecc 3:11).; Spirit-birth pictured by the wind (Joh 3:8).; Plans perish when the breath departs (Psa 146:4) — breath and thought.; Bread strengthens the heart (Judg 19:5; Psa 104:15), yet food "enters not his heart but his stomach" (Mar 7:19), and the heart should be strengthened "by grace, not by foods" (Heb 13:9). Three verses, three angles on the same relation.; The bosom holds both loved ones and anger or insults (Ecc 7:9; Psa 89:50).; "Conscience" also = "consciousness / mindful" (Heb 10:2; 1Pe 2:19).

17283.text: 4. Fringe observations collected (quick list): God's own heart and soul (§3.10).

17284.text: a. Tag/surface misalignment. The following rows point the Strong's tag at an English word that is not its equivalent. The tag is probably right at verse level, but the "surface" should not be used as a gloss [verify]: Exo 28:3 "whom"; Exo 35:34–35 "him / them"; Gen 31:20 "Laban"; Pro 23:34 "midst"; Pro 30:19 "high"; Psa 73:21 "soul" on H3824; Lam 1:16 "spirit" on H5315G; Gen 34:3 "tenderly"; Gen 17:14 "shall"; Jer 19:9 "and"; Mic 2:7 "Has the"; Lev 23:30 "whoever/person"; Gen 27:25 "and"; Rev 16:3 "thing"; Deu 27:25 "blood"; Pro 6:16 "to him"; Psa 106:15 "among them"; Gen 46:15 "altogether"; Jer 11:20 "mind"; Isa 44:19 "considers"; Pro 15:32 "intelligence"; Est 7:5 "dared"; Job 6:11 "patient"

17287.text: d. Missing from M47, but clearly inner-seat vocabulary in the English text: kidneys ("heart and mind", Jer 11:20 etc.); bowels / stomach (Lam 1:20); *nous* "mind" (1Co 14:14; Rom 7:25; Eph 4:23; brief §4 says M15); "inner being / inner self" (Eph 3:16; 2Co 4:16); "bones" (repeatedly paired with heart and spirit); "compassion" (Hos 11:8); [verify] which clusters hold these.

17289.text: 3. (a) Why the verses were not narrated: The reason is the same as for M47. The M25 units read the life and death words. The desire side of each verse was left for this strand. The M25 ledgers often quote the verse in full, but they quote it for its life or death word: Psa 34:12, "desires life", is quoted for "long days" (LD-101).; Joh 4:14, "never be thirsty again", is quoted for "living water" (LD-121).; Ecc 5:18, "find enjoyment", is quoted for "life enjoyed, as given" (LD-115). That ledger line was woven into Ch 2. 10.6 gained Ecc 2:24–26 in the M47 pass, but not the three verses that say the same thing (3:12; 5:18; 8:15).; Three verses (Exo 14:12, Psa 34:12, Pro 8:35–36) also have a Ch 2 side. I first treated Ch 2 as closed to them. That was my over-reading of OT-08, corrected in §6.

17290.text: 10.6 *Wanting* | v11 | Given section headings. New: *Through the eye* (Gen 2:9, 3:6; Ecc 7:26), enjoyment given and the rich fool compared (Ecc 3:12, 5:18–20, 6:12, 8:15), heat (Isa 57:5), *Wanting that owns the one who wants* (Tit 3:3–5, 2:11–14; Luk 8:14; Pro 23:35), unmet wanting (Hag 1:6; Isa 29:8; Exo 17:3 against Judg 15:18; Eze 23:21–22), *Shaped by fear* (Jer 42; Exo 14:12), *Wanting life* (Psa 34:10–14; 1Pe 3:9–10; Job 7:7), *Aimed at God* (Psa 27; 16; 119:37, 40), *Thirst answered* (Joh 4, 6; Jer 2:13), *A person* (Song 2:7, 3:5, 8:4–7, 5:2–6), *Jealousy and envy* (1Ki 19; Num 11:29; Psa 73; Pro 23:17–18; Jam 3:13–16), *Taken away* (Joe 1:5), *Possessions* (Mat 19:22; Pro 15:27), delight list (Psa 119:75–77; 68:30)

17291.text: 10.7 *Choosing and setting direction* | v20 | Mat 19 (and the Isaiah 1 "one place" sentence restated); Joh 5:40–44; Ruth 3:10–13, 4:4–6; 2Ti 3:11–12; Joh 21:18–22; 2Ch 19:2–3; Pro 14:13–14; Dan 11:25; Isa 47:13–14

17294.text: 13.4 *Nature* | v2 | First content: God's look on what he made (Gen 1:21, 25, 31); the creatures' thirst met (Psa 104:10–15, 27–28; 42:1); the ostrich (Job 39:14–17)

17295.text: 10.10 *Relating to others* | v15 | 1Sa 19:1–7 in *Loyalty and honour*; Deu 19:6 in *Anger between people*; new *Friends, company and care* (Job 6:15–18; Ecc 4:9–11; Job 31:19–20; Job 17:8–9 against 31:29–30; Pro 10:12; Song 2:7)

17296.text: 10.9 *Relating to God* | v16 | Psa 73:3, 20 with 73:16–17; new *Waiting, and pleading* (Lam 3:24–26; Hezekiah, Isa 38:2–5); *Calling on God to wake* rewritten from a summary into the grounds of each call, Bildad, and Isaiah's call answered (51:9, 17; 52:1; 64:7–8), Psa 57:6–8, Judg 5:12

17300.text: Ch 6 | v12 | The stirred spirit widened (Ezr 1:5; Hag 1:6, 12–14; 1Ch 5:25–26; Jer 51:11)

17304.text: Ch 11 | v21 | §4: five new faces (eat-drink-be-merry; jealousy; rousing oneself; the redeemer's will; whom the need is spoken to) and Haggai's order. §5: three more voices (Lam 3:24; Psa 57:8; Pro 6:22)

17307.text: 3. (a) Why the verses were not narrated: There is one main reason. The M47 reset narrated the seat words (heart, soul, spirit, flesh) and left the desire side of each verse to a later strand. This is that strand. So 10.6 *Wanting* was short (38 lines). It had nothing on: desire in the heart through the eye (Mat 5:28; Pro 6:25); delight and its objects (Psa 119:70; Isa 55:2; Pro 18:2; Psa 40:14); the wilderness craving (Num 11); evil desire (Pro 21:10; Psa 10:3; Mic 7:3); longing for people (1Th 2:17; Rom 1:11); what is desired being taken away (Eze 24:21, 25); Ch 5 had no account of a life held precious (1Sa 26:21; 2Ki 1:13–14; Pro 6:26; Psa 49:7–8).; Two smaller reasons:

17309.text: Ch 11 cited around a verse. It cites "Psalm 10:2, 4" and skips 10:3, "the wicked boasts of the desires of his soul".

17311.text: Ecclesiastes answers its own vanity. 10.6 had only the "striving after wind". The same book names envy as the source of toil (4:4), sets "a handful of quietness" against it (4:6), and names enjoyment as "from the hand of God" (2:24–26). Ch 11 §2 gains the merry heart that God approves (Ecc 9:7). Until now the merry heart was shown only as a threshold of danger.

17314.text: 5. (c) Errors realigned: Ch 5, "exhaustion". Ch 5 v3 called Job 10:1, Ecc 2:17 and Jon 4:3 "a third kind of hating one's life, which is exhaustion rather than discipleship". The verses give their own ground: Job: bitterness of soul; the Preacher: "what is done under the sun was grievous to me"; Jonah: anger that God spared Nineveh (4:1–4); faintness comes only with the second wish (4:8); The frame came from M47 batch G §6. Ch 5 now gives each ground. Ch 2 already read Jonah correctly.; Ch 4, Pro 21:1. It was listed among the "materials" for the state a heart is in. It is a heart being directed, "wherever he will", and "will" is the delight word. It is now set apart in Ch 4 and placed in 13.1 *Delight*.

17315.text: OT-95, jealousy (8 verses). Elijah's zeal (1Ki 19:10, 14), God's jealousy (Eze 36:5), heart envy (Pro 23:17; Jam 3:14), Jam 4:5, Num 11:29 and Eze 8:3. Jealousy has faces that differ by whose it is (God's, a husband's, envy of sinners). It needs one account, from the jealousy words, rather than pieces now.

17410.text: Seeing, coveting, taking.: Achan, in his own words: *"when I saw among the spoil a beautiful cloak … then I coveted them and took them. 17854.text: 3. Envy of the wicked, and the future (10.6 *Jealousy and envy*): Proverbs has the same pairing twice, and both times it answers with the future: *"Fret not yourself because of evildoers, and be not envious of the wicked, for the evil man has no future"* (Pro 24:19–20); *"Surely there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off"* (23:18, already in 10.6); Just before 24:19 stands *"Do not rejoice when your enemy falls, and let not your heart be glad when he stumbles"* (24:17). Envy of the wicked who prosper, and gladness when an enemy falls, are set two verses apart. Job disowns the second in his oath (10.10).

17856.text: 4. Jealousy as not yet grown (10.6 *Jealousy and envy*): *"But I, brothers, could not address you as spiritual people, but as people of the flesh, as infants in Christ. I fed you with milk … for while there is jealousy and strife among you, are you not of the flesh and behaving only in a human way? For when one says, 'I follow Paul,' and another, 'I follow Apollos'"* (1Co 3:1–4).; The figure is infancy. Jealousy is named as the sign of not having grown. It shows in attaching oneself to a favourite teacher.; Compare 1Pe 2:2, already in 10.6: *"Like newborn infants, long for the pure spiritual milk, that by it you may grow up"*. One infancy longs for milk in order to grow. The other stays on milk and quarrels.; *"The night is far gone … Let us walk properly as in the daytime … not in quarreling and jealousy. But put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the flesh, to gratify its desires"* (Rom 13:12–14). Before it: *"the hour has come for you to wake from sleep"* (13:11).; The figure is waking at daybreak. Jealousy belongs to the night.; The answer is a garment, "put on", not a stronger will. It goes with refusing to make "provision" for the flesh's desires.

"Never be thirsty again" describes a want met at its source, and the source is "in him".

17945.text: Death precious in his sight. *"Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints"* (Psa 116:15). The psalmist had been in *"the snares of death"* (116:3) and was delivered (116:8). He answers *"You have loosed my bonds"* (116:16).: Compare Ezekiel. God has no pleasure in the death of the wicked, yet the death of his saints is precious.; The word is not delight. It is "precious, weighty". I read: not glad of it, but not careless of it. A saint's death costs something in God's sight.; Compare Ch 5: Saul says to David, *"my life was precious in your eyes this day"* (1Sa 26:21). It is the same word, once between two men and once in the Lord's sight.

The answer: *"If it is my will that he remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me!"* (21:22).

17982.text: 3.1 "If it pleases the king": a request put under another's pleasure (Neh 2:5, 7; Est 1:19; 5:4; 9:13): 10.7 *Whose measure* already asks in whose eyes a choice is good, and has "The king's eyes, or God's" (1Sa 14:36) and "Another's will, given the whole decision" (Est 3:9, 11; 8:8). These five verses are the same words from the asking side. In each, *ṭôb* names the king's own judgement: literally "if it is good to the king". The asker puts the request under the king's pleasure. The roles: the M18 word is the measure; "king" (M72) is standalone, the one whose pleasure decides. The verses differ in what stands behind the ask.

18114.text: Jealousy for another (1Ki 19:10, 14; Num 11:29).: Elijah says the same words twice, word for word: *"I have been very jealous for the Lord, the God of hosts … and I, even I only, am left, and they seek my life, to take it away"*. The first time is in the cave (19:10). The second is after the wind, the earthquake, the fire and "the sound of a low whisper" (19:12–14).; The encounter did not change how he described himself.; God does not argue with him. He gives him work: *"Go, return on your way … you shall anoint"* (19:15–16).; His zeal is joined in the same sentence to being alone and to his life being hunted. I read zeal for God that has turned into the sense of standing alone. God answers it with work, not with a correction.; Joshua's is also jealousy for another: *"Are you jealous for my sake? Would that all the Lord's people were prophets, that the Lord would put his Spirit on them!"* (Num 11:29). It is refused by the very person it is for.

18117.text: Jealousy among the wise (Jam 3:14–16). *"But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast and be false to the truth. This is not the wisdom that comes down from above, but is earthly, unspiritual, demonic. For where jealousy and selfish ambition exist, there will be disorder and every vile practice."*: It is set against *"Who is wise and understanding among you?"* (3:13). So it is the jealousy of people who would be counted wise.; "Bitter" is a taste. Psalm 73 has "embittered" too.; It is "in your hearts", and it shows outwardly as "disorder".; James names its source in three words. The middle one, "unspiritual", is literally "soulish".

18119.text: Roused after long restraint: *"The Lord goes out like a mighty man, like a man of war he stirs up his zeal … For a long time I have held my peace; I have kept still and restrained myself; now I will cry out like a woman in labor; I will gasp and pant"* (Isa 42:13–14). Explore the figures. In two verses God's zeal is a warrior and a woman giving birth. I read zeal that both fights and brings forth, held back a long time and then released with a cry. Isaiah sets the two pictures side by side. The joining is his.

18163.text: Toward building. *"the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, so that he made a proclamation"* (Ezr 1:1; 2Ch 36:22). Then *"everyone whose spirit God had stirred to go up"* (Ezr 1:5). Not everyone went: the stirred ones rose. Haggai gives the order: They *"obeyed the voice of the Lord … And the people feared the Lord"* (Hag 1:12).; *"I am with you, declares the Lord"* (1:13).; *"And the Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel … and the spirit of all the remnant of the people. And they came and worked"* (1:14).; The stirring follows obedience, fear and a word of presence, and it ends in work. Of Cyrus: *"I have stirred him up in righteousness … he shall build my city and set my exiles free, not for price or reward"* (Isa 45:13).

18164.text: Toward destroying.: *"So the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria"*, after *"they broke faith with the God of their fathers"* (1Ch 5:25–26); *"the Lord stirred up against Jehoram the anger of the Philistines"* (2Ch 21:16), after a written warning (21:12–15); *"I will stir up the spirit of a destroyer against Babylon"* (Jer 51:1); *"The Lord has stirred up the spirit of the kings of the Medes, because his purpose concerning Babylon is to destroy it"* (51:11); Each time the verses give the ground: broken faith, a king's sin, or his purpose and vengeance for his temple.

18173.text: Rousing oneself rightly, and wrongly (Job 17:8; 31:29): *"The upright are appalled at this, and the innocent stirs himself up against the godless. 18267.text: "Die" and "death" (H4191, H4194, G0599, G2288) move between: the body's end ("and he died", Gen 5); a sentence passed by people ("shall surely be put to death", Lev 20); a judgement from God (Gen 38:7; 2Sa 6:7); the end of a way taken ("its end is the way to death", Pro 14:12); something that happens inside a living person ("sin came alive and I died", Rom 7:9; "abides in death", 1Jo 3:14; Nabal's heart, 1Sa 25:37); a power that reigns, holds and is destroyed (Rom 5:14; Act 2:24; 1Cor 15:26); a death undergone on purpose ("died to sin", Rom 6:2; "I died to the law", Gal 2:19); a death that belongs to the Lord ("if we die, we die to the Lord", Rom 14:8); What differs is what produces the death and who acts in it. The verses name sin (Rom 5:12; Jam 1:15), vexation and jealousy (Job 5:2), the sluggard's desire (Pro 21:25), God (Deu 32:39) and Christ, who "tastes death for everyone" (Heb 2:9). The word stays the same. *(R: the grouping is mine; each verse names its own cause.)*

18337.text: Who rouses, and whom. God rouses himself (Zec 2:13). People call on God to rouse himself (Psa 44:23). God rouses a human spirit (Ezr 1:1). God rouses people against people (2Ch 21:16; Eze 23:22). A person rouses himself, or does not (Isa 64:7). Hatred rouses strife (Pro 10:12). An angel rouses a prophet from sleep (Zec 4:1). Love is not to be roused before its time (Song 2:7).

18338.text: Toward what. The same verb rouses toward building (Ezr 1:5; Hag 1:14), toward destruction (Jer 51:1, 11), toward praise (Psa 57:8; Judg 5:12), toward hearing (Isa 50:4), and toward strife (Pro 10:12).

18339.text: What cannot be roused. The dead man "till the heavens are no more" (Job 14:12), and the idol with "no breath at all in it" (Hab 2:19). Leviathan, whom "no one is so fierce that he dares to stir … up" (Job 41:10), stands outside the inner being and stays in the data.

18368.text: The soul is said to die. "Let me die the death of the upright, and let my end be like his!" "Let me die with the Philistines." In both, the Hebrew is *let my soul die*. "Behold, all souls are mine … the soul who sins shall die." Elijah "asked that he might die" (literally, asked for his soul to die), and so did Jonah.

18369.text: Delivered from death: counted. Of 15 verses in the pull where a soul is delivered, brought up, kept back, ransomed, saved or not abandoned from death, Sheol or the pit, 12 speak of a living person kept from dying or brought back from near it (Psa 30:3; 33:19; 56:13; 86:13; 116:8; Jos 2:13; Job 33:18, 28, 30; Isa 38:17; Jam 5:20; Pro 23:14, where the child "will not die", 23:13). 2 look beyond death (Q2-04, Q2-05). 1 says no man can do it: "Who can deliver his soul from the power of Sheol?" (Psa 89:48).

18378.text: G5591 *psychikos* ("natural, of the soul") | "natural body" (1Cor 15:44, 46) · "The natural person does not accept the things of the Spirit of God" (1Cor 2:14) · "earthly, unspiritual, demonic" wisdom (Jam 3:15) · "worldly people, devoid of the Spirit" (Jude 19) | Of the body, it is simply the first order, sown before the spiritual: no blame. 18386.text: Four contrasts, sown and raised. "What is sown is perishable; what is raised is imperishable. It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power. It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body." "It is not the spiritual that is first but the natural, and then the spiritual."

18389.text: The risen Christ's own body. "See my hands and my feet, that it is I myself. Touch me, and see. For a spirit does not have flesh and bones as you see that I have" — said because "they … thought they saw a spirit". He ate fish before them; the apostles "ate and drank with him after he rose". Thomas: "put out your hand, and place it in my side". Yet he also came and "stood among them" with "the doors being locked", "vanished from their sight", and was at first not recognised (Mary, the Emmaus pair, the disciples at the lake).

18390.text: Like his body. "our citizenship is in heaven, and from it we await a Savior … who will transform our lowly body to be like his glorious body, by the power that enables him even to subject all things to himself." "predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son". "what we will be has not yet appeared; but we know that when he appears we shall be like him, because we shall see him as he is."

18394.text: C. Notes the narrative must not smooth over: Flesh and bones / flesh and blood. Luke 24:39 has the risen Christ saying a spirit "does not have flesh and bones as you see that I have". 1 Corinthians 15:50 says "flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God". Both are stated. No verse reconciles them, and I would quote both and stop (rule 69).; "Spiritual body." The verse sets *psychikos* against *pneumatikos* (§A). It does not say what a spiritual body is made of. Any gloss ("not immaterial but Spirit-governed", or the opposite) would be "I read", and I'd suggest leaving it out. Q4-08 is the nearest Scripture comes to showing one.; Between death and rising. "away from the body and at home with the Lord" (2Cor 5:8) belongs to Q2 / OT-03 ("After death"), not here. Signpost only.

The lost sheep, coin and son of Luk 15 (15:4, 8, 24, 32), "to seek and to save the lost" (Luk 19:10), "should not perish" (Joh 3:16), and the lost sheep of Israel (Psa 119:176; Jer 50:6; Eze 34:4, 16; Mat 10:6; 15:24). In Luk 15:24 the father sets "dead" beside "lost". Woven in *Death spoken of in more than one way*.; Perishing as a present state, set against being saved. 1Co 1:18; 2Co 2:15; 4:3; 2Th 2:10, with its stated cause: "because they refused to love the truth". Set against it is eternal life (Joh 3:16; 10:28). Woven in the same subsection.; Inner things perish. Hope (Job 8:13; Pro 10:28; Lam 3:18; Eze 19:5; 37:11), courage, literally the heart (Jer 4:9), wisdom and counsel (Isa 29:14; Jer 49:7; Eze 7:26), truth (Jer 7:28), and the heart corrupted by a bribe (Ecc 7:7). Woven in *Death in the living*.; One person destroying another. 1Co 8:11; Rom 14:15. Woven in *Death in the living*, with a pointer to 10.10.; Stated causes of perishing. Forgetting God and serving other gods (Deu 8:19–20; 30:18; Jos 23:16); not repenting (Luk 13:3, 5); not believing (Jude 5); desires to be rich (1Ti 6:9); "those who are far from you shall perish" (Psa 73:27); taking the sword (Mat 26:52); false witness (Pro 19:9; 21:28). Luk 13:3 and 2Th 2:10 are woven. The rest are carried by the death-in-the-living causes and stay here as sources for when those strands are read.; Readiness. 18653.text: c1. The inner acts toward the resurrection: 34 verses (A1). This is the largest group.: *Denied*, and the ground Jesus gives: "the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit" (Act 23:8); Jesus' answer: "You are wrong, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God"; (Mat 22:29; Mar 12:24). He grounds it in God's name: "the God of Abraham" (Mar 12:26), "for; all live to him" (Luk 20:38); The section cites only Mat 22:30 and Luk 20:36, on marriage.; *Questioned, and not understood until later:*; "questioning what this rising from the dead might mean" (Mar 9:10); "as yet they did not understand the Scripture, that he must rise from the dead" (Joh 20:9); "When therefore he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this,; and they believed" (Joh 2:22); "Then he opened their minds to understand the Scriptures" (Luk 24:45–46); "Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead" (2Ti 2:8); *Known and believed:*; Martha: "I know that he will rise again in the resurrection on the last day" (Joh 11:24); then "Do you believe this?" "Yes, Lord; I believe" (11:26–27); *Mocked, deferred, thought incredible:*; "some mocked. But others said, 'We will hear you again about this'" (Act 17:32); "Why is it thought incredible by any of you that God raises the dead?" (Act 26:8); "the hope and the resurrection of the dead" on trial (Act 23:6; 24:21); *Faith emptied if it is not so:*; "how can some of you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?" (1Co 15:12); "your faith is futile and you are still in your sins" (15:17); "If in Christ we have hope in this life only, we are of all people most to be pitied" (15:19,; cited in *Life weighed*); The section cites none of 1Co 15:12–19. Faith (M13, OT-05.19) is a handle here.; *Upset:* "saying that the resurrection has already happened. They are upsetting the faith of; some" (2Ti 2:18).; *Feared, and a conscience stirred:*; the guards "lest his disciples … tell the people, 'He has risen from the dead'" (Mat 27:64); Herod: "John, whom I beheaded, has been raised" (Mar 6:16); "he was perplexed" (Luk 9:7); "that is why these miraculous powers are at work in him" (Mat 14:2); I read Herod's word as his own guilt speaking, since it names the beheading.
