20434.text: What was approved (the four decisions): Method. Every strand ledger gets a "Change of character" section. For each word or concept with more than one face, record: the faces and their verses; the circumstances that differ: who thinks · toward or against whom · joined with what · heart state · alone or with counsel · setting · what follows or comes back · narrative context; why, stated by the verse or as a labelled reading; Words are pulled by word across all clusters, never by cluster.; Narrative. Each operation section (10.x) gets a passage on when this activity changes character, and why. Ch 11 §4 ("One word, opposite values") grows into the cross-cutting account of what governs change. It stays open for later strands.; Reopen OT-H2. Weave discussion §11: flow 3, thoughts acting on the self: Job 20:2; Dan 7:28; flow 5, consequences returning to the one who devised: Est 9:25; Ps 10:2; Jer 6:19; Pro 21:5; These go into 10.3 and 10.0.; Build. Complete the change-of-character section for every thought word, then weave it in.

20436.text: Ledger OT-H2. I held the discussion's §11 ("thought as a system", six directions of flow) as "superseded by 10.0". Two of its flows reached the narrative only in part, and two not at all: Flow 3 — thoughts acting on the self: "my thoughts answer me, because of my haste within me" (Job 20:2); "my thoughts greatly alarmed me" (Dan 7:28). Not woven.; Flow 5 — consequences returning to the one who devised: Haman's "evil plan … should return on his own head" (Est 9:25); "the fruit of their devices" (Jer 6:19, quoted in 10.2 but not for this point); "let them be caught in the schemes that they have devised" (Ps 10:2); "the plans of the diligent lead surely to abundance" (Pro 21:5). Not woven.

20438.text: Face: Discretion; Verses: Pro 1:4; 2:11; 3:21; 5:2; 8:12; Who thinks: the young, the son, wisdom herself; Joined with / aimed at: knowledge, prudence, sound wisdom. It "watch[es] over you" (Pro 2:11)

20439.text: Face: Evil device; Verses: Pro 12:2; 14:17; 24:8; Ps 10:2, 4; 21:11; 37:7; 139:20; Job 21:27; Jer 11:15; Who thinks: the wicked, the schemer, enemies; Joined with / aimed at: arrogance (Ps 10:2), pride (10:4), quick temper (Pro 14:17); aimed *against* the poor, against God, against "you"

20440.text: Face: God's purpose; Verses: Jer 23:20; 30:24; 51:11; Job 42:2; Who thinks: God; Joined with / aimed at: "the intents of his heart"; cannot be thwarted

20443.text: Face: God's plans; Verses: Jer 29:11; Ps 33:11; 40:5; 92:5; Isa 55:8–9; Mic 4:12; 2Sa 14:14 ("devises means")

20454.text: 2. Thoughts arise before they are chosen. Several verses describe thoughts that happen *to* the person: Ezekiel 38:10 has two stages: "thoughts will come into your mind, and you will devise an evil scheme." First something rises, then the person works on it. [lexical] The Hebrew there is *dᵉvārîm* (H1697, "words" or "things"), literally "things will come up on your heart."; In Job 20:2, "my thoughts answer me, because of my haste within me." The thoughts *respond to* an inner state.; In Daniel 7:28, "my thoughts greatly alarmed me." The thoughts act on the person.; In Romans 2:15, "conflicting thoughts accuse or even excuse them." They are like inner voices arguing with each other.; So in these verses the person is both where thoughts come from and on the receiving end of them.

20455.text: 4. Knowing a thought is separate from producing it. 1 Corinthians 2:11 says only "the spirit of that person" knows a person's thoughts, and only God's Spirit knows God's. Separately, God searches and knows human thoughts (Psalm 139:23; 1 Chronicles 28:9; Psalm 94:11; 1 Corinthians 3:20), and so does Jesus (Luke 5:22, 6:8, 11:17; Matthew 9:4, 12:25).: *Caveat:* in 1 Corinthians 2:11 the Strong's number is G3588, the Greek article. The word "thoughts" is supplied by the translation; the Greek says "the things of a person."

20456.text: 4.2 What thoughts are: Inner speech. 21 of the rows (H0559, *ʾāmar*, "to say") are places where the Hebrew says "he *said*" and the ESV renders it "he thought," as in 1 Samuel 18:11: "Saul thought, 'I will pin David…'" The Greek *dialogismos* (G1261) and *logismos* (G3053) are also built on *logos*, "word" [lexical]. In these texts, to think is to speak inwardly. *Caveat:* how many rows show this depends on the ESV's choices.; Devising or planning. H4284 *maḥăšāvāh* (from H2803 *ḥāšav*, "to devise"). These thoughts are designs with a direction. They can be just (Proverbs 12:5), evil (Isaiah 59:7), or God's own plan (Micah 4:12). Because they point somewhere, they can be judged, and they can be abandoned (Isaiah 55:7).; Likening, or interpreting. H1819 *dāmāh* ("to resemble") is used in Psalm 50:21: "you thought that I was one like yourself." Many rows record thoughts that were wrong: Genesis 38:15, Mark 6:49, Luke 24:37, Matthew 20:10, Acts 12:9, Judges 3:24 and 2 Kings 5:11. So a thought is a reading of reality, not reality itself.; Something that grows and matures. 1 Corinthians 13:11: "I thought like a child … I gave up childish ways."; Transient, yet weighty. Human thoughts are "but a breath" (Psalm 94:11) and "futile" (1 Corinthians 3:20). Yet God weighs them (Proverbs 15:26), and before the flood they were the measure of human wickedness (Genesis 6:5). God's thoughts, by contrast, are "very deep" (Psalm 92:5), "vast" (Psalm 139:17) and "higher" (Isaiah 55:8–9).

20469.text: Craft: Exodus 31:4 and 35:32–35 ("to devise artistic designs", "skilled designer"), 2 Chronicles 2:14 ("execute any design"), 2 Chronicles 26:15 ("invented by skillful men").

20470.text: Evil schemes: Esther 9:25 (Haman's "evil plan"), Jeremiah 18:18, Proverbs 6:18.

20471.text: God: Jeremiah 29:11, Psalm 33:11 ("the plans of his heart"), 2 Samuel 14:14 ("he devises means").

20474.text: Written on by God: Hebrews 8:10 and 10:16, where the pairing of "hearts" and "minds" is reversed between the two verses.

20481.text: 1. The heart or mind is the place thoughts come from. Mark 7:21 and Matt 15:19 ("out of the heart come evil thoughts"). Also: "a heart that devises wicked plans" (Prov 6:18); "plan evil things in their heart" (Ps 140:2); "devise evil … in your heart" (Zech 7:10; 8:17); "The heart of man plans his way" (Prov 16:9); "his heart does not so think; but it is in his heart to destroy" (Isa 10:7); "the reasoning of their hearts" (Luke 9:47); In Jer 4:14, thoughts *lodge* within: "How long shall your wicked thoughts lodge within you?" This follows the call to "wash your heart."

20482.text: 2. Thoughts arrive, often at night.: "as you lay in bed came thoughts of what would be" (Dan 2:29); "thoughts from visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men" (Job 4:13); "thoughts will come into your mind" (Ezek 38:10); "doubts arise in your hearts" (Luke 24:38); "an argument arose among them" (Luke 9:46); In Dan 2:29–30, the thoughts that come in the night are tied to revelation: "he who reveals mysteries made known to you."

20483.text: 3. The bed is also where people devise deliberately.: "He plots trouble while on his bed" (Ps 36:4); "devise wickedness … on their beds! When the morning dawns, they perform it, because it is in the power of their hand" (Mic 2:1); The same place hosts thoughts that come unbidden (Dan 2:29) and thoughts that are worked on on purpose (Ps 36:4).

20484.text: By God: he writes his laws on minds and hearts (Heb 8:10; 10:16) and fills craftsmen with skill "to devise artistic designs" (Exod 35:32–35).

20485.text: By instruction: Proverbs is written "to give … discretion (*mᵊzimmāh*) to the youth" (Prov 1:4), and Wisdom "find[s] … discretion" (Prov 8:12).

20489.text: 9.2 What thoughts are: Design: forming something that does not yet exist. H2803G (19 rows) describes craftsmanship: cherubim "skillfully worked" (Exod 26:1, 31) and "skilled design" (Exod 39:3). The faculty itself is neutral. *Maḥăšāvāh* covers both artistry and plots, and *mᵊzimmāh* covers both "discretion" (Prov 2:11) and "evil devices" (Prov 12:2). What makes a thought good or evil is what it is designed toward.; Reckoning: giving something its value or category. H2803H/J (60 rows): Human misreckoning: Eli "took her to be a drunken woman" (1 Sam 1:13), "we esteemed him stricken" and "we esteemed him not" (Isa 53:3–4), Judah "thought she was a prostitute" (Gen 38:15).; God's reckoning: "he counted it to him as righteousness" (Gen 15:6), "the Lord counts no iniquity" (Ps 32:2), and the nations "accounted as the dust on the scales" (Isa 40:15, 17).; To think is to judge the worth of something, and people can judge wrongly.; Inner speech.; "all his thoughts are, 'There is no God'" (Ps 10:4). The thought is quoted as a sentence.; Hannah "was speaking in her heart; only her lips moved" (1 Sam 1:13).; *Dialogismos* covers both inner reasoning and outward "argument", "quarreling" and "disputing".; "conflicting thoughts accuse or even excuse" (Rom 2:15).; Something that affects the body and emotions.; "his thoughts alarmed him; his limbs gave way, and his knees knocked together" (Dan 5:6; also 4:19; 5:10; 7:28).; "the cares of my heart" (Ps 94:19), and "haste within me" (Job 20:2).; A divided mind stalls a person: "limping between two different opinions" (1 Kgs 18:21, H5587A).; Creaturely and passing.; "but a breath" (Ps 94:11).; "When his breath departs … on that very day his plans perish" (Ps 146:4).; "futile" (1 Cor 3:20; Rom 1:21).; "striving of heart … striving after wind" (Eccl 2:22; 4:16).; Fully open to God.; "you discern my thoughts from afar" (Ps 139:2); also Ps 139:23; 1 Chr 28:9; "I know their works and their thoughts" (Isa 66:18); Heb 4:12.; Jesus knows people's thoughts (Luke 5:22; 6:8; 9:47; 11:17; Matt 9:4; 12:25).

20490.text: 9.3 From thought to action (Claude's reading): The verses trace a path from thought to deed: Arising. Thoughts come, often in the night (Dan 2:29; Job 4:13; Ezek 38:10; Luke 24:38).; Lodging. They stay and are dwelt on (Jer 4:14).; Reckoning. They weigh up and value things (Isa 53:4; 1 Sam 1:13).; Devising. They take the form of a plan (Ezek 38:10b; Ps 36:4).; Expression. Tongue, lips and eyes: "your tongue plots" (Ps 52:2), "devise words of deceit" (Ps 35:20), "winks his eyes plans" (Prov 16:30), "whisper … imagine the worst" (Ps 41:7).; Action. Hand and feet: "when the morning dawns, they perform it" (Mic 2:1); "a heart that devises … feet that make haste" (Prov 6:18); "their feet run to evil … their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity" (Isa 59:7).; The same path also runs toward good: "When I think on my ways, I turn my feet to your testimonies" (Ps 119:59).

20491.text: Where responsibility sits. The commands address the stages from lodging onward: "forsake … his thoughts" (Isa 55:7); "let none of you devise evil" (Zech 7:10); "take every thought captive" (2 Cor 10:5); "wash your heart" (Jer 4:14); The *arising* is not commanded, but it is not neutral either. What comes up shows the condition of the heart (Gen 6:5; Mark 7:21). So thoughts that arise reveal the heart, and devising engages the will. The heart itself can be changed from outside: written on, given discretion, guarded, or darkened.

20493.text: 1. Outward: heart → speech → body → action.: "a heart that devises wicked plans, feet that make haste" (Prov 6:18); "your tongue plots" (Ps 52:2); "winks his eyes plans" (Prov 16:30); "when the morning dawns, they perform it, because it is in the power of their hand" (Mic 2:1)

20494.text: 2. Inward: outside influences → heart and mind.: God writes on minds and hearts (Heb 8:10; 10:16) and fills people with skill (Exod 35:35).; Instruction gives discretion (Prov 1:4).; Counsel establishes plans (Prov 15:22; 20:18).; The serpent leads thoughts astray (2 Cor 11:3), and "the god of this world" blinds (2 Cor 4:4).

20497.text: 5. Back again: consequences returning to the one who devised.: "his evil plan … should return on his own head" (Esth 9:25); "the fruit of their devices" (Jer 6:19); "let them be caught in the schemes that they have devised" (Ps 10:2); "The plans of the diligent lead surely to abundance" (Prov 21:5)

20506.text: The heart is where thoughts come from: Mat 15:19 / Mar 7:21; Pro 6:18 (§9.1.1): Ch 3 "The heart is the source"; Ch 12 (Gen 6:5, Mat 15:19)

20509.text: The source is shaped from outside: God writes on minds (Heb 8:10); minds blinded (2Co 4:4) (§9.1.4): Ch 11 §1 "The inner being is acted upon as much as it acts"

20514.text: 3. New — not yet in any chapter: The path from thought to deed (§9.3). Arising (Dan 2:29; Job 4:13; Luk 24:38) → lodging (Jer 4:14) → reckoning (Isa 53:4) → devising (Ps 36:4) → expression through tongue, lips and eyes (Ps 52:2; Pro 16:30) → action through hand and feet (Mic 2:1; Pro 6:18; Isa 59:7). The same path runs toward good: "When I think on my ways, I turn my feet to your testimonies" (Ps 119:59). Commands address the stages from lodging onward. Arising is not commanded, but it shows the state of the heart.; Thinking as reckoning, i.e. assigning worth (§9.2.2). Human misreckoning (Gen 38:15; 1Sa 1:13; Isa 53:3–4) against God's reckoning (Gen 15:6; Ps 32:2; Isa 40:15, 17). This links directly to justification language. It has no home in the narrative yet.; Thoughts that arrive, especially at night (§9.1.2–3). The bed is where thoughts come unbidden (Dan 2:29) and also where people plot on purpose (Ps 36:4; Mic 2:1). The night thoughts are tied to revelation (Dan 2:29–30).; Thought moves the body (§9.2.4). "his thoughts alarmed him; his limbs gave way" (Dan 5:6); the divided mind "limping between two different opinions" (1Ki 18:21). This fits Ch 6 (flesh) or Ch 11 §3 ("The parts give way in sequence").; Outbound hearing: God hears the plots (§13.1). "You have heard their taunts … all their plots" (Lam 3:61); Mal 3:16. The narrative has hearing only as the inbound way in. Your comment in the discussion: *"Yes, hearing is an integral part of the outbound thought."*; Design and craft as the good form of devising (§9.2.1). Exod 26:1; 35:32–35: God fills craftsmen with skill "to devise artistic designs".

20516.text:
What the heart says is mostly a verdict: about God's seeing, about self, about the future. Kinds seen:
• denial that God sees (Ps 10:11, 13; Zep 1:12; Isa 47:10)
• self-exaltation (Isa 14:13; 47:8; Zep 2:15; Obd 3; Eze 28:2)
• self-credit (Deu 8:17; 9:4)
• fear (Deu 7:17; 1Sa 27:1)
• enquiry (Ecc 1:16; 2:1, 15; 3:17–18; Deu 18:21; Jer 13:22)
• denial of God (Ps 14:1; 53:1)

20534.text: Face: Devising against; Verses: Psa 36:4; 52:2; 41:7; 35:4, 20; 21:11; 140:2, 4; 10:2; Mic 2:1; Eze 11:2; 38:10; Nah 1:9, 11; Neh 6:2, 6; Jer 11:19; 18:18; 48:2; Est 8:3; 9:24–25; 1Sa 18:25; 2Sa 14:13; Dan 11:24–25; Hos 7:15; Pro 16:30; 24:8; Zec 7:10; 8:17; Gen 50:20a; What differs: Aimed against a named person or God, nearly every time. Joined with arrogance (Psa 10:2), whispering together (41:7), tongue and lips (52:2; Pro 16:30), the bed (Psa 36:4; Mic 2:1), envy of a rival (1Sa 18:25, after the anger of 18:8). Against the one who trained them: "Although I trained and strengthened their arms, yet they devise evil against me" (Hos 7:15); Why (basis): The "against" is stated (S). Ingratitude turns into a plot (S, Hos 7:15)

20535.text: Face: God devising against, conditionally; Verses: Jer 18:8, 11; 26:3; 36:3; Mic 2:3; Jer 49:20, 30; 50:45; Lam 2:8; What differs: God devises "against", but: "Return, every one from his evil way" (18:11); "It may be they will listen … that I may relent of the disaster that I intend" (26:3); Why (basis): God's "against" is aimed at turning, and it is open to change. "Against" alone does not make thinking evil (S)

20536.text: Face: God devising for; Verses: Jer 29:11; 2Sa 14:14; Gen 50:20b; What differs: "plans for welfare and not for evil" (Jer 29:11); "he devises means so that the banished one will not remain an outcast" (2Sa 14:14); Why (basis): For whom God thinks: the exile, the banished (S)

20538.text: Own devices against God's outstretched hands: "I spread out my hands all the day to a rebellious people, who walk in a way that is not good, following their own devices" (Isa 65:2).

20543.text: Quick temper and evil devices in one proverb: "A man of quick temper acts foolishly, and a man of evil devices is hated" (Pro 14:17). Temper and scheming are set side by side. This is a link to the anger strand.

20553.text: Face: Devising and plotting; Verses: Pro 24:2; Psa 38:12; 2:1; Isa 59:3, 13; What differs: Fixed on violence or treachery, "all day long"; "the nations rage and the peoples plot" (Psa 2:1): plotting stands beside rage

20555.text: Face: A growl, and its absence; Verses: Isa 31:4; Psa 115:7; Isa 8:19; What differs: God as a lion growling over his prey, "not terrified" (protective); idols that "do not make a sound in their throat"; mediums who "mutter"

20565.text: *dialogizomai / dialogismos* | Honest troubled reasoning · hardened anxious reasoning · inner questioning seen by Jesus · reasoning together into murder · self-talk of the rich man · quarrel, dispute, opinions · argument about greatness · futile thinking · evil thoughts from the heart · partiality: "judges with evil thoughts" · thoughts revealed by the child set for a sign | Luk 1:29 · Mar 8:16–17; Mat 16:7–8 · Mar 2:6, 8; Luk 5:21–22; 6:8; 9:47 · Luk 20:14; Mat 21:25 · Luk 12:17 · 1Ti 2:8 ("without anger or quarreling"); Phili 2:14; Rom 14:1 · Luk 9:46 · Rom 1:21; 1Co 3:20 · Mar 7:21; Mat 15:19 · Jam 2:4 · Luk 2:35 | Inner reasoning becomes outward quarrel when it is shared and set on one's own standing (Luk 9:46; Rom 14:1) (R). The heart state decides honest or hardened (Luk 1:29 against Mar 8:17, S). In 1Ti 2:8 the quarrel word stands beside anger, a link to the anger strand

20566.text: *dianoia* | The mind given wholly to love God · the mind hostile · the mind darkened because of hardness of heart · the mind's desires, "children of wrath" · proud in the thoughts of their hearts · laws written on minds · minds prepared · a sincere mind stirred · understanding given | Mat 22:37; Mar 12:30; Luk 10:27 · Col 1:21 · Eph 4:18 · Eph 2:3 · Luk 1:51 · Heb 8:10; 10:16 · 1Pe 1:13 · 2Pe 3:1 · 1Jo 5:20 | Eph 4:18 states the causal direction: "darkened in their understanding … due to their hardness of heart." The heart's state changes the mind's character (S). Eph 2:3 links the mind's desires to wrath (anger strand)

20570.text: 2 | Toward or against whom | Confirmed; the strongest marker in the data | "against" is stated in nearly every plotting verse. Contradicted as a sole test: God's "against" is not evil, and is aimed at turning (Jer 18:11; Mic 2:3 after 2:1). What decides is the *purpose* of the against

20816.text: The verb puts a question to a person for information (tree H7592 1a1 'to ask, ask for', 1a3 'to enquire, enquire of').

20817.text: The asking is a pursuit: he seeks to learn something from her.

20818.text: What he asks is whose daughter she is, her family.

20819.text: The servant asks; Rebekah is the one asked and she answers him.

20820.text: The servant is telling how it went at the spring, after she had given him and his camels drink (Gen 24:45-46).

20821.text: The servant asked Rebekah to name her family.

20822.text: He asked, she named her father and grandfather, and then he gave her the ring and bracelets.

20823.text: He asks to learn whether she belongs to his master's kin.

20824.text: Discovery: the purpose behind the question is read from verse 48; the passage is needed to settle it.

20905.text: The verb puts a question about the cause of a state (tree H7592 1a1 'to ask, ask for', 1a3 'to enquire').

20906.text: Downcast, said of faces, is the look of sorrow shown in the face (tree H7451, bad, unpleasant, giving pain, unhappiness).

20907.text: The asking is a pursuit: Joseph seeks the reason for what he sees.

20908.text: What he asks about is why their faces are downcast.

20909.text: What is downcast is their faces, the outward show of their state.

20910.text: Joseph asks; Pharaoh's officers in custody are the ones asked.

20911.text: The officers' faces are downcast; Joseph is the one who sees it and asks.

20912.text: Joseph has seen that they were troubled (Gen 40:6) and they are confined in his master's house.

20913.text: Joseph asked the officers the reason for their downcast faces.

20914.text: The officers' faces show sorrow today.

20915.text: Joseph asks why their faces are downcast, and they answer that they have dreamed and no one interprets (Gen 40:8).

20916.text: The downcast faces prompt his question: the question names the faces as what he asks about.

20917.text: Discovery: what lies behind the downcast faces is not stated in this verse; the passage gives their answer (Gen 40:8).

20940.text: The verb is asking for something as a favour (tree H7592 1a2 'to ask (as a favour), borrow'), here asking neighbours for goods.

20941.text: The asking is a pursuit: each woman is to seek goods from her neighbour.

20942.text: What is asked for is silver and gold articles and clothing.

20943.text: The asking ends in plunder: the Egyptians are stripped of these things.

20944.text: Each Israelite woman asks; her neighbour and the Egyptians are the ones asked.

20945.text: These are God's words of what will happen when the people go out of Egypt (Exo 3:20-21).

20946.text: Each woman is told to ask her neighbour and the woman in her house for goods.

20947.text: They ask, they put what they receive on their sons and daughters, and so they plunder the Egyptians.

20948.text: The favour God gives the people in the sight of the Egyptians is what the asking draws on.

20949.text: Discovery: what the asking amounts to, a request granted or a borrowing, the claims process tests against the other verses of this asking.

21056.text: The verb is a demand put as a question: what the Lord asks of Israel (tree H7592 1a1 'to ask, ask for').

21057.text: Fear here is reverent awe before the Lord (tree H3372 1a3 'to fear, reverence, honour, respect').

21058.text: Ways here is the figure for the course of a life lived toward the Lord (tree H1870 1e 'of course of life (fig.)').

21059.text: Love here is love of a person toward God (tree H0157 1a3 'human love for or to God').

21060.text: Serve here is the service of the Lord (tree H5647 1a4 'to serve (God)').

21061.text: Heart and soul together say that the service is given with the whole inner seat (tree H3824 1a2 'heart (of man)'; H5315 1a 'the inner being of man').

21062.text: The Lord's asking is a pursuit: he looks for something from Israel.

21063.text: The fear is required, a pursuit set before Israel.

21064.text: The walking in his ways is required, a pursuit set before Israel.

21065.text: The love is required, a pursuit set before Israel.

21066.text: The service is required, a pursuit set before Israel.

21067.text: What the Lord asks is four things: to fear him, to walk in his ways, to love him and to serve him.

21068.text: The one feared is the Lord their God.

21069.text: The ways are the Lord's: the course he sets for them.

21070.text: The one loved is the Lord.

21071.text: The one served is the Lord their God.

21072.text: Walking is the outward act of the ways: living by the course the Lord sets.

21073.text: The Lord asks; Israel is the one asked.

21074.text: Israel is to fear the Lord, who is the one feared.

21075.text: Israel is to walk in the Lord's ways and to love him.

21076.text: Israel is to serve the Lord.

21077.text: The speaker turns to this after recalling forty days on the mountain and the Lord's unwillingness to destroy them (Deu 10:10-11).

21078.text: The Lord asks Israel for four things.

21079.text: Israel is to fear the Lord.

21080.text: Israel is to live by the Lord's ways.

21081.text: Israel is to love the Lord.

21082.text: Israel is to serve the Lord with the whole inner seat.

21083.text: The one question is answered by four infinitives: to fear, to walk, to love and to serve.

21084.text: The four are one requirement, not four separate ones.

21085.text: The question states what the Lord requires; it is not asked to gain information.

21086.text: Discovery: other verses join fear, love, walking and service; the claims process tests how the four relate across them.

21222.text: The verb is a close questioning of a captive for what he knows (tree H7592 1a3 'to enquire, enquire of').

21223.text: The questioning is a pursuit: he seeks the names from the captive.

21224.text: What the questioning draws out is the names of the town's leaders, a count of seventy-seven.

21225.text: The answer takes a written form: the names are written down for him.

21226.text: He questions; the young man of Succoth is the one questioned.

21227.text: Gideon has returned from battle and captured the two kings of Midian (Judg 8:12-13), and now captures a young man.

21228.text: He questioned the captured young man about Succoth.

21229.text: He captures a young man, questions him, and has the names of Succoth's leaders written down.

21230.text: The questioning is aimed at those who hold authority in the town.

21231.text: Discovery: what he does with the names is not stated here; the passage shows it (Judg 8:15-16).

21267.text: The verb is a greeting inquiry after a man's state (tree H7592 1a3 'to enquire, enquire of').

21268.text: The asking is a pursuit of word on the Levite's state.

21269.text: What they asked about is the Levite's welfare.

21270.text: The asking comes with their turning aside and coming to his house.

21271.text: The five men ask; the young Levite at Micah's house is the one asked.

21272.text: The five men have passed on to the hill country of Ephraim and come to Micah's house (Judg 18:13), where one of them has spoken of the images (Judg 18:14).

21273.text: The five men asked the young Levite how he fared.

21274.text: They turn aside, come to the Levite's house, and ask after his welfare; then they stand at the gate (Judg 18:16).

21275.text: The asking is a greeting that opens the visit.

21276.text: Discovery: what the men do next at the house is told in the verses that follow (Judg 18:16-17); the passage is needed.

21278.text: Aloud here only carries a public announcement or summons; no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21279.text: Aloud, negated, gives withheld voice: the sigh of grief is to be kept inward and not voiced.

21281.text: Quiet here is only the state of a land, a realm, a sea, a place or a weapon (peace after war, calm water); it names no inner-being operation.

21282.text: Quiet gives a peaceable nature: a calm and gentle disposition of a spirit, a life, a house, or a people, named by another word.

21283.text: Quiet is the inner calm and stillness of a person or God: a chosen or given settledness, or its refusal, that the verse commands, praises, laments the lack of, or promises.

21285.text: Quiet gives security: a people or person settled, unthreatened and without fear, named by another word of the verse.

21290.text: Quietness is itself the settled inner rest and trust: the result of righteousness, the ground of strength, and better than toil and striving.

21296.text: Being silent is a person's, or God's, holding back of speech for a reason the verse shows: submission, fear, shame, awe, wisdom, obedience, waiting, or failure to speak up; or the refusal of it (anguish, praise, the watchmen's duty).

21298.text: Silent here is only the absence of voice in a thing or an enforced muteness and names no inner-being operation of the surface.

21301.text: Call is a purposeful act of the inner being turned to God: calling or crying out to the Lord, or on his name, in need, trust, praise or worship, or refusing to.

21304.text: Call is God's own act of summoning, choosing or appointing a person or people; it bears on their inner response (faith, obedience, hope), which other words of the verse name, and is the outward act upon them.

21306.text: Call here only names, designates or labels a person, place or thing (to be called such a name, to call it so); no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21308.text: Call is here the judgement a person puts on a thing in naming it (calling evil good, the Sabbath a delight, a fast acceptable): a valuing of the heart voiced in speech.

21309.text: Call is here a public proclamation, summons or announcement to others; it is the outward act and bears on the hearers, with no inner-being operation of the caller named.

21311.text: Called here only names, designates or labels a person, place or thing (to be called such a name, to call it so); no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21313.text: Called is here the outward act of summoning, addressing or sending for another person or thing; it bears on the other's response but names no inner-being operation of the one who calls.

21314.text: Called is the standing given by God's call (the vocation); it is what diligence, worthiness or walking is directed at, not an inner operation in itself.

21315.text: Called is God's own act of summoning, choosing or appointing a person or people; it bears on their inner response (faith, obedience, hope), which other words of the verse name, and is the outward act upon them.

21316.text: Called is here a public proclamation, summons or announcement to others; it is the outward act and bears on the hearers, with no inner-being operation of the caller named.

21319.text: Calling is the standing given by God's call (the vocation); it is what diligence, worthiness or walking is directed at, not an inner operation in itself.

21322.text: Calling is here the outward act of summoning, addressing or sending for another person or thing; it bears on the other's response but names no inner-being operation of the one who calls.

21326.text: Calls is a purposeful act of the inner being turned to God: calling or crying out to the Lord, or on his name, in need, trust, praise or worship, or refusing to.

21327.text: Calls is here the outward act of summoning, addressing or sending for another person or thing; it bears on the other's response but names no inner-being operation of the one who calls.

21328.text: Calls is God's own act of summoning, choosing or appointing a person or people; it bears on their inner response (faith, obedience, hope), which other words of the verse name, and is the outward act upon them.

21340.text: Called, negated, gives a disclaimed standing: the person judges himself unworthy to be called so, a humility of the heart.

21346.text: Deal is here the outward act of dealing with a person, with a disposition (kindness, loyalty, honesty, courage or good faith) named by another word of the verse; it bears on the one dealt with and names no inner operation of its own.

21349.text: Deal here only handles, manages or settles a matter, a treaty or a plain term of dealing; no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21354.text: Dealt is here the outward act of dealing with a person, with a disposition (kindness, loyalty, honesty, courage or good faith) named by another word of the verse; it bears on the one dealt with and names no inner operation of its own.

21355.text: Dealt is here the outward act of dealing with a person in hatred, fury, violence or by what they deserve, named by another word of the verse; it bears on the one dealt with and names no inner operation of its own.

21356.text: Dealt is God's own act of dealing with a person or people according to what they are or have done, or according to his own faithfulness or love; it bears on them and is the outward act upon them.

21359.text: Offer here is the ritual or narrated presenting of an offering, a prescribed or reported act with no inner-being operation named by it.

21362.text: Offer is here an offering made to a party other than the Lord (an idol, a demon, the dead or a man); it is the outward act of worship, and its devotion is named by other words of the verse, if at all.

21363.text: Offer here carries no inner-being operation: it is a figure of nature or an outward act of commerce.

21365.text: Offered here is the ritual or narrated presenting of an offering, a prescribed or reported act with no inner-being operation named by it.

21368.text: Offered is here an offering made to a party other than the Lord (an idol, a demon, the dead or a man); it is the outward act of worship, and its devotion is named by other words of the verse, if at all.

21376.text: Fresh here describes a thing, a time or a figure (a new garment, a new cart, fresh water, an old pool, a parable of wineskins); no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21379.text: New here describes a thing, a time or a figure (a new garment, a new cart, fresh water, an old pool, a parable of wineskins); no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21383.text: New gives newness to the heart or spirit: a changed condition of the seat of the person, which the verse sets against the heart of stone or against transgression.

21384.text: New gives freshness to a song of praise: the praise of the person is voiced afresh to the Lord.

21386.text: Old here states an age, an old age or an age class (years old, an old man, young and old, the older brother); no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21390.text: Old here dates a thing to the past (of old, the days of old, from of old) or names the people or prophets of old; no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21391.text: Old here describes a thing, a time or a figure (a new garment, a new cart, fresh water, an old pool, a parable of wineskins); no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21392.text: Old is here the older person toward whom respect, mercy or rebuke is directed; it names the party the act is aimed at, and the act is named by another word of the verse.

21393.text: Old is here the former time (the days of old, the things of old) as what remembering, considering or comfort is directed at; the inner act is named by another word of the verse.
